works.name: Adaptive Experimentation Can Hide Model Error: Detection Limits and Falsification Budget
works.summary: Bounds model-adequacy detection in stationary, finite-action/outcome settings using the experimenter’s sampling distribution. Separates absent acquisition evidence from a detector’s failure to capture available signal. An expansion-relative diagnostic motivates reserving actions for falsification. Empirical evidence is mixed: the primary comparison fails detection eligibility, revisions depend on horizon, and measured-data replay retains fit-derived labels. Small selected LLM pilots and incomplete campaigns do not establish general scientific-reasoning gains.

works.name: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
works.summary: Combines paper-derived skills and parallel hypothesis investigations to deliver drug-discovery candidates. Evaluations cover 121 decision questions, three LLM-graded process tasks, and three selected studies followed by human assays. LpxH activity/binding and cytokine-signaling inhibition do not confirm the proposed binding site, covalency, or JAK1 selectivity. An anonymized target study and differing tool/skill access limit scrutiny and component attribution; learning from experimental outcomes remains future work.

works.name: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
works.summary: Accelerates evolutionary program search with batched latent agents, KV-cache communication, and hidden-state diversity filtering. Across 21 numerical tasks it evaluates more programs per hour than three text-based frameworks. Ablations show early search benefits, while zero-agent variants approach similar final scores. Improvements over historical AlphaEvolve constructions do not establish new global records, and fixed numerical evaluations provide limited evidence of broader scientific generalization.

works.name: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
works.summary: Coordinates dataset discovery, quality screening, and code-based transformation for scientific RAG and instruction tuning. Biomedical and chemistry benchmarks support useful corpus construction, with smaller gains for chemistry retrieval than fine-tuning. Efficiency comparisons use measured pipeline runtime against expert time estimates. Reported overlap controls reduce contamination risk, while derived sources, dataset-level quality judgments, and corpus composition limit claims of verified scientific knowledge or autonomous discovery.

works.name: CLEAR: Structured Specifications for Controllable Long-Horizon ML Research Engineering
works.summary: Converts papers and task descriptions into structured execution specifications, then uses a planner, coding workers, and localized repairs to construct ML pipelines. Evaluation covers PaperBench and MLE-Bench Lite; a matched-backbone specification ablation supports the intermediate representation. Other comparisons change model backbones as well as orchestration, limiting causal claims about heterogeneous routing. The optional human specification checkpoint was not used in reported runs.

works.name: FrontierPhysics
works.summary: A benchmark of 56 physics research tasks designed by 42 physicists from their own projects. Agents select methods, produce numerical artifacts and write manuscripts, assessed through deterministic verifiers and expert-authored rubrics applied by a reviewing agent. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, the best passes 46 of 168 trials. Expert trajectory audits expose reasoning and intuition failures, alongside residual evaluation errors; detailed diagnoses apply to the audited model–harness cohort.

works.name: A semi-autonomous multi-agent pipeline for high-energy astrophysics research with enforced provenance and verifiable self-extension
works.summary: Builds reusable astronomy tools behind deterministic checks and cross-model review, while requiring reported numbers to occur in recorded outputs or carry paper locators. On a planted-defect benchmark, the combined checks stop 64 of 65 defects but reject 40 of 69 correct controls. IXPE studies include qualified reproduction and null results. Provenance does not ensure scientific correctness; statistical and source-mixing errors survive the checks.

works.name: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
works.summary: Packages expert defect-calculation protocols as reusable prompts for VASP setup, convergence checks, finite-size corrections, formation energies, and thermodynamic analysis. A BaCd2P2 demonstration covers seven defect species but requires researcher intervention on restart diagnosis, directory mapping, and substitution of a custom solver. The run informed prompt refinement; it does not establish held-out reliability or detailed defect-physics validation. Reference scripts and calculation data are linked.

works.name: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?
works.summary: Compares persistent and reset research agents on matched streams across nine ML task families. Persistent state improves early search efficiency, largely through faster or stronger initialization; only one agent shows a substantial aggregate final-performance gain. Matched insight cards do not consistently beat shuffled cards. Short fixed streams, mostly single paired runs, and bundled code–context retention limit claims about scientific learning across tasks.

works.name: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness
works.summary: Demonstrates revised display-control software, spectral feedback, and response-model refinement in one optical see-through color-matching setup. An acknowledged RGB-hold interface passes 12 live control checks. Feedback improves five targets; a separate model revision helps seven of nine paired contexts, with two regressions. The error bound assumes uniform model accuracy and global optimization, neither established by sampled prediction scores; cross-goal transfer and general hardware redesign remain untested.

works.name: Verifier strength does not buy discovery quality: a pre-registered two-domain test of LLM-based automated research, with post-hoc evidence pointing to proposer-pool composition
works.summary: Re-gates fixed LLM and random proposal pools through three verifier tiers in scheduling and simulated edge offloading. Under author-reported frozen criteria, stricter filtering does not produce the predicted held-out ordering. Weak and standard gates usually select identical candidates. Exploratory pool merging helps only scheduling and also doubles proposal count. One 0.5B proposer, overlapping source instances, weak tier separation, and an unreachable strict-order criterion limit generalization.

works.name: Are LLM Research Agents Reliable Judges of Predictability? Evidence from Planted-Signal Worlds
works.summary: Tests forecasting agents in simulated worlds with known predictive structure, separating their verdicts from sealed-holdout performance. Initial bootstrap worlds contain an exploitable repeated-value artifact; Gaussian-shock follow-ups still show frequent unsupported predictability claims and framing sensitivity. At matched false-positive rates, agents do not outperform conventional tests consistently. The brief leaves the decision threshold unspecified, and stronger baseline comparisons are exploratory.

works.name: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
works.summary: Compares expert-guided and unattended agents for translating and designing warm-rain parameterizations in JAX. Most gains concern executable, differentiable, mass-conserving closures; only two of 100 four-round candidates beat the best retuned physical baseline on rain-mass error. Expert-guided neural-ODE development required 131 prompts and remained less accurate. Missing source equations affect one translation test; box-model results do not establish coupled-climate performance.

works.name: Cloudra: Geometric Reasoning and Scientific Validation for Autonomous Reaction Mechanism Exploration
works.summary: Connects chemical species and reaction steps to geometric operations, quantum-chemical calculations, and explicit physical checks. Same-backbone comparisons on 50 mechanism tasks favour guided workflows, particularly in pathway support. Published scores use human reconstruction of run artifacts; full self-consistency concerns delivered objects rather than all requested steps. Electronic-energy agreement, computation cost, incomplete pathways, and method-limited negative conclusions require separate interpretation.

works.name: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents
works.summary: Builds procedural skills and reference catalogs from scientific-software documentation, then revises them using execution failures and fresh-session validation. ScienceBoard-VE separates 108 evolution tasks from 168 repaired test tasks. Gains demonstrate transfer across related operations in six applications; a stronger model gains only 2.11 percentage points. Resource coverage, information volume, and routing differ across baselines, limiting claims about knowledge organization alone.

works.name: Towards AI-Agent-Accelerated Research in High-Energy Physics: A Case Study in Monte Carlo Analysis
works.summary: Studies agent-assisted reconstruction and extension of a CEPC Bell-observable analysis through simulation, frozen definitions, deterministic checks, and diagnostic controls. Humans authorize state-changing work and retain scientific interpretation. The benchmark uses instructions rather than an information-access barrier, and the enlarged sample reuses development seeds. Four correlated selections are not independent replications. Active human time was not prospectively recorded, so no measured productivity speed-up is established.

works.name: The Verifier Is Part of the Simulator: Evidence-View Gaming in Agentic Equation Discovery
works.summary: Studies equation-discovery agents that choose which numerical summary reaches a fixed verifier. Across simulated PDEs, score-based view selection can reject correct libraries or accept equations missing diffusion without altering data or verifier code. Prescribed agreement reduces some errors but abstains more; a fixed fine view outperforms it on PDEBench. Three-model prompt experiments are single-turn selection tests, distinct from the deterministic attack and negative transfer results.

works.name: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
works.summary: Coordinates question selection, theoretical derivation, computational checks, and nitrogen-vacancy spin experiments through agents that can reject or revise collaborators’ work. An acquisition agreeing with predictions was classified inconclusive after drift controls failed; a revised protocol passed retained criteria on four withheld targets. One configured laboratory and human-built apparatus bound the evidence. The public Auctopus engine excludes study prompts and instrument descriptions; experimental data and analysis code are request-only.

works.name: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents
works.summary: Reanalyzes numerical claims in agent-written papers and distinguishes values unsupported by the recorded experiment from values absent from available artifacts. A deterministic context-and-decoy checker achieves high precision but limited recall on a small held-out human-labeled sample. Most uncertified claims remain traceable. Shared retrieval candidates, annotation revisions, incomplete large-run coverage, and changes to both judge model and harness constrain the conclusions.

works.name: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents
works.summary: Extracts global checks, problem-level approaches, and implementation lessons from completed coding attempts, then selectively injects relevant experience and review advice during execution. Comparisons span numerical solvers, GPU kernels, and scientific software repair. Memory banks are frozen before evaluation; transfer is tested between two kernel benchmarks using one agent and model family. Reported coding gains do not establish continual learning or end-to-end scientific discovery.

works.name: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
works.summary: Introduces LongChang, where agents choose investigations and construct apparatus in simulated worlds with altered physical laws. Separate agents generate scenes and judge reports against hidden laws and exploration records. Evaluation distinguishes law correctness from experimental support and compares guidance, turn budgets, and apparatus access. Findings concern fixed simulated scenes and model-based judgments, not discovery of unknown real-world laws or independently validated scientific results.

works.name: Do AI Scientists Know What's New?
works.summary: Audits proposal-level novelty checks and introduces ClaimNov, which extracts contribution claims, retrieves comparable prior claims, and produces evidence-linked novelty judgments. Tests distinguish disguised papers, disputed contributions, later-realized ideas, and mixed proposals. Results depend on fixed reference pools, heuristic novelty labels, and LLM generation and judging; they do not establish open-literature search completeness or better completed research.

works.name: OpenFrontiers-Bench
works.summary: Combines dated research-problem records with a Lean-graded mathematics benchmark. Evaluation on 50 selected items separates closed-book rediscovery from live-web recovery of published solutions. Most web successes retrieve known solutions, and clean evaluation sets differ by model lineage and cutoff. Corpus records are not deduplicated conjectures; status labels and AI-reviewed formalizations still require source scrutiny.

works.name: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
works.summary: Extracts perovskite-device records under versioned annotation and equivalence rules, calibrates verifiers against experts, and attaches category-level reliability to the database. Retrospective prediction uses a held-out publication year. The multi-agent discovery dialogue is illustrative, with selected held-out recipes, rather than a validated discovery experiment. Deployment reliability remains model-judged, and category accuracy does not establish confidence in individual values.

works.name: Auto-Research Arena
works.summary: Evaluates autonomous research harnesses across nine language-model efficiency objectives, separating quality and resource admissibility from target improvement. Records all launched experiments, including failures, and scores the best admissible candidate. Comparisons include six LLM-based harnesses and a restricted non-agentic baseline; simple sequential search remains competitive. Results concern compact pretraining programs, a fixed data pool and training seed, and specified hardware, rather than general scientific discovery.

works.name: EmbodiedLab
works.summary: Evaluates robot agents on 30 simulated experiments requiring manipulation, instrument readings, analysis, and evidence-linked answers. Success also requires restoring the bench. The best native-interface agent succeeds in 43.3% of tasks; interaction and restoration dominate attributed failures. Added skills reuse successful runs on the same experiments and serve a diagnostic comparison. Familiar simulator physics and coupled model–harness configurations limit generalization.

works.name: Labference
works.summary: A robotic-laboratory benchmark protocol connecting observed physical outcomes to subsequent operation choices, with separate selection, execution and completion measures. It defines controlled state pairs and matched support interventions across spatial, numerical and memory-dependent tasks. Current quantitative results concern initial simulated easy weighing; matched Oracle studies and wider task-family evaluation remain pending. Physical-robot recordings provide qualitative pilot examples.

works.name: SciValidityBench
works.summary: Generates experimental histories from 64 task specifications to test whether remembered evidence may validly guide a decision. Programmatic oracles and paired corruption, repair, and counterfactual controls distinguish retrieving a fact from using its governing context. Tests span five validity mechanisms and six domain settings. Results concern controlled decision tasks and explicit state compilation; transfer to real laboratory histories or end-to-end research remains open.

works.name: PersonaScienceBench
works.summary: Adapts 200 tasks from five benchmarks into interactions with simulated researchers while keeping each task’s objectives fixed across persona settings. Measures task performance, fact recovery and repetition. Actor and simulator share a model, so comparisons concern coupled systems. Most conditions have one rollout; incomplete outcomes and heterogeneous aggregation restrict scoreboard comparisons. The four profiles are contrasting configurations rather than representative human populations.

works.name: POSEIDON: Scaling Training Environments for Scientific Agents from Code Repositories
works.summary: Turns scientific repositories into reproduction, subflow, completion, and correction tasks using executable seed programs and iterative validation. The resulting Pearl collection supports supervised agent training, evaluated on six benchmark suites. A separate 600-environment human audit examines quality. Reported transfer depends on repository selection, generated evaluators, and benchmark exclusions; sample auditing does not certify every environment or establish autonomous scientific discovery.

works.name: SCI-AGENT-EXAM
works.summary: A workflow-oriented benchmark of 120 expert-curated tasks across 11 fields and seven research activities. Agents must deliver executable outputs and scientific reports, evaluated through weighted deterministic checks and expert-authored rubrics applied by an LLM judge. Ten-model experiments show that report quality and executable correctness can diverge; trajectory snapshots further expose regressions. Scores describe the specified offline tasks and harness, with judge calibration bounded by the documented reference checks.

works.name: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
works.summary: Combines retrieval of historical scientific designs, evolving start-selection strategies, and optimizer-program evolution under physical constraints. The authors evaluate gravitational-wave detector designs on eight held-out topologies using a differentiable simulator and matched scientific evaluation budgets. Results support optimization within this setting; transfer beyond simulation and dependence on historical-library coverage remain open.

works.name: GeoAgent: Contract-Constrained LLM Agents for Seismic Data Processing
works.summary: Connects seismic-processing tools through a fixed nine-stage graph, with explicit contracts for artifacts, input resolution, parameter ownership, and output validation. Deterministic geometry checks address failures that prompting alone did not prevent. Evidence comes from engineering measurements on one dataset and model family; adaptive planning, migration quality, and broader controlled comparisons remain unestablished.

works.name: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
works.summary: Trains text and vision models to predict acceptance from anonymized manuscripts, with stronger matched-source results from page images. ICLR inputs include rebuttal-era revisions, while arXiv rejection labels are inferred from missing proceedings matches. Accuracy concentrates at rating extremes and degrades across sources. The score estimates review outcomes; it does not establish correctness, novelty, or scientific impact.

works.name: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
works.summary: Audits research trajectories with separate Analyzer and Verifier agents, then tests runtime feedback against matched unassisted runs. Its taxonomy covers 14 integrity violations. Reported findings depend on LLM judgments and mathematics/ML tasks; testing files and extra resources remain accessible deliberately, so detected violation rates should not be generalized to environments enforcing those boundaries.

works.name: Astro2Method
works.summary: Tests ML-method selection on 500 expert-reviewed questions from 346 astronomy papers. Historical-paper retrieval and additional reasoning yield no consistent overall gain. Web-search improvements concentrate in cases retrieving the source paper, while method-masked pipeline context improves harder questions. Difficulty reflects completeness of source explanations; public-paper exposure and privileged pipeline information limit claims about prospective scientific reasoning.

works.name: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
works.summary: Extracts interpretable idea factors from archived programs whose score differences remain unexplained, then uses bandit-selected edits and plateau-triggered exploration to guide program evolution. Evaluations cover eleven mathematical tasks and six machine-learning engineering tasks. Reported gains concern bounded executable objectives; the theoretical benefits require stated assumptions, and transfer to expensive scientific verification remains untested.

works.name: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents
works.summary: Learns continuous reference solutions and constructs matching PDE problems through manufactured solutions, giving coding agents numerical feedback without solving every new reference problem. Evaluations cover Navier–Stokes and Vlasov–Poisson-type tasks and adaptations of existing PDE agents. Its reliability analysis assumes controlled distribution mismatch and independent evaluation data; success on generated problems does not establish accuracy across arbitrary physical regimes.

works.name: Recursive Flint
works.summary: An open-weight mixture-of-experts coding model built with Recursive’s Eureka Machine and a human team. The model card specifies 39.8B total parameters and approximately 2.5B active per token, including the output head. Included as a concrete automated-research output and reusable coding component; released weights and inference code do not independently validate the development process or reported performance.

works.name: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
works.summary: Studies frontier coding agents improving scientific ML baselines in Agent4Sci, separating optimization, held-out evaluation, and trajectory auditing. Default gains are largely engineering-driven; targeted research skills produce more varied interventions. The study distinguishes metric improvement from scientific insight, with limitations from run variance, imperfect audits, task-specific skills, and the absence of a human-researcher baseline.

works.name: Autonomous adaptive spectral analysis with an LLM agent for self-driving laboratories
works.summary: Uses an LLM to inspect spectra and diagnostics, adjust predefined fitting parameters within bounded retries, or abstain, while deterministic code calculates the physical quantity. On 203 archived film spectra, it retains 183 baseline values, recovers 16 failed analyses, and abstains on four. This retrospective, single-campaign study does not test live laboratory control or detection of physically incorrect results that pass numerical checks.

works.name: Bayesian Model Discovery with Language Models: Closing the Loop between Hypotheses and Experiments
works.summary: Combines LLM-proposed functional forms with numerical parameter fitting, evidence-weighted predictions, and experiment selection by joint information gain over models and parameters. Four benchmarks compare predictive error and structural recovery, with ablations of numerical feedback. Results depend on the candidate pool, priors, and observation model; containing the true law as a special case is explicitly distinguished from recovering its exact form.

works.name: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
works.summary: Combines computational chemistry tools with session records, confirmed project knowledge, and human-reviewed rules reused across projects. Four case studies and controlled replays of four internal tasks examine the contribution of retained context. The authors explicitly position it as supervised research assistance; campaign-wide memory benefits remain unisolated, and complete docking records include unreleased collaborator results.

works.name: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Extracts atomic claims from published cancer-registry studies, executes reproduction analyses, and tests alternative analytical choices through agent-generated perturbations. SEER-Repro supplies the evaluation setting. The authors distinguish reproducing reported findings from assessing their sensitivity; flagged alternatives require expert review, and report-based grading does not independently verify the complete analysis code.

works.name: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
works.summary: Develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent search, converts selected plans into Harbor tasks, and uses contribution-weighted offline model training and fixed-model workflow replay for later runs. DFM-Bench scores proposals and research histories. Automated investigation-design gains coexist with declining novelty and importance; retrospective publication correspondence is sensitive to retrieval and group differences. Compiled plans do not establish completed, independently validated discoveries.

works.name: PhysClosureBench
works.summary: Provides 50 physics research tasks with specified goals and constraints. A 20-criterion score measures local accomplishments, while a separate closure assessment tests whether essential evidence and applicability conditions resolve the research question. Model-based grading includes a selected human consistency check; high partial scores are not equivalent to complete scientific closure.

works.name: SciPIvot
works.summary: A scientific-judgment benchmark built from 248 human corrections across 26 research projects. Models choose between an original agent plan and a human-corrected alternative using the earlier project record. Five models often retain corrected mistakes, and added context or reconsideration does not consistently help. The challenge-set design evaluates recognition of selected corrections, rather than autonomous planning or the frequency of failures in research.

works.name: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
works.summary: Coordinates coding agents through typed hypothesis contracts, sandboxed experiments, shared memory, retrospective ablations, and evidence-linked manuscript audits. Evaluation includes 70 computational ML campaigns scored by an AI-reviewer proxy and separate held-out case studies. Its single accepted ALIFE paper involved substantial human specification, verification, statistical analysis, and editing; automated rubric gates also missed evaluation-protocol changes.

works.name: Brilliance for adaptive computational research in accelerator physics
works.summary: Combines reusable physics modules, agent-written programs, and JuTrack calculations to revise accelerator investigations. Cases include ideal storage-ring design and offline calibration against measured responses with a specialist reference. Detailed requests and further scientist guidance supply expertise. The sub-10-pm candidate retains momentum-acceptance limitations; finite tracking and single configuration comparisons do not establish operational readiness. Calibration agreement is not unique recovery of machine errors or residuals at measurement resolution.

works.name: AutoSciBench: Autonomous Benchmark Generation for Evaluating Scientific Agents
works.summary: Constructs scientific-agent tasks from high-level concepts and executable recipes, then revises them using solver trajectories and judge feedback. Experience from earlier refinements guides later generation across computational biology, materials science, and clinical imaging. The generator also serves as solver during refinement, and quality ratings come from LLM judges. Increased difficulty and favorable ratings do not independently establish scientific validity or broad evaluation coverage.

works.name: Can AI Scientists Coordinate at Runtime?
works.summary: Lets current agents choose authorized host capabilities at runtime, with optional scoped contracts and advisory artifact checks. A single-seed study of three hosts finds the highest ResearchClawBench means with runtime selection alone; contracts plus verification reduce those means. Verification does not block transitions, budget matching is not fully reconciled, and an exploratory DiscoveryBench subset gives different rankings.

works.name: Denario Project: Deep Knowledge Artificial Intelligence Agents for Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Provides modular agents for ideation, literature checks, analysis, code execution, and paper drafting across supplied scientific datasets. Its journal tutorial evaluates heterogeneous drafts through team expert self-assessment, with substantial prompt and verification roles for humans. Outputs require expert development; documented failures include silent synthetic-data substitution, unsupported citations, missing solvers and invented results. The interdisciplinary demonstration is a single case.

works.name: Agentic AI–Physicist Collaboration in Experimental Particle Physics: A Proof-of-Concept Measurement with LEP Open Data
works.summary: Demonstrates an agent-assisted thrust analysis of archived ALEPH data, using supplied prior analyses, code execution, unfolding and manuscript drafting. Physicists define acceptance criteria, inspect outputs and approve scientific decisions. This is a supervised demonstration of a known observable, with no controlled productivity comparison; the paper’s descriptions of response-Monte-Carlo covariance and total uncertainty combination remain internally inconsistent.

works.name: ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI
works.summary: Coordinates limitation-driven hypotheses, subset-to-full experiments, ablation-based refinement, and simulated review–rebuttal cycles that can trigger supplementary experiments. Across 107 selected ML-paper challenges, it reports 86 successful improvements; gains and most review scores condition on those successes. Acceptance figures come from automated reviewers, with a 33-paper human assessment; reported cost averages about $3,765 per completed NeurIPS-derived task.

works.name: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
works.summary: Provides a biomedical workspace that couples instruction/skill-harness revision with model reinforcement learning. Case studies report fixed-model adaptation, fixed-harness pass@4 gains, and three alternating update cycles on scientific QA tasks. Real researcher interactions illustrate task and rubric construction; the controlled adaptation experiment uses bounded simulated feedback, and individual feedback or skill contributions are not isolated.

works.name: IdeaForecastBench
works.summary: Evaluates whether ideas proposed from literature available before a cutoff correspond to later publications. It contains 624 rolling episodes across 52 topics, generates up to five ranked ideas, and reports separate judge results. This measures research forecasting under a retrospective protocol; broad or generic predictions and judge sensitivity complicate interpretation as precise scientific anticipation.

works.name: ResearchStudio
works.summary: Microsoft’s ResearchStudio provides Idea for literature-grounded proposal development and Reel for editable posters, narrated videos, blogs, and an aligned viewer. Idea is assessed through automated proposal judgments; Reel’s quantitative study covers posters, while other outputs remain capability demonstrations. Their shared repository supports distinct research stages rather than establishing a fully autonomous experimental discovery pipeline.

works.name: Recursive Eureka Machine
works.summary: Recursive describes an automated research loop that proposes ideas, implements experiments, checks results, and carries useful context across parallel investigations. Public examples include training and GPU-kernel optimization; its later Flint model provides a released development outcome. Available research artifacts support inspection of selected outputs, but do not establish access to the complete research framework or independently verified autonomy.

works.name: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
works.summary: Examines whether language models can assess methodological soundness before experiments are run. Results-masked proposals receive reviewer-derived proxy labels and separate expert judgments on a subset. Standard prompts favor approval, while aggressive prompts trade false approvals for false rejections. The study concerns proposal-stage judgment; its labels do not establish experimental truth or general research quality.

works.name: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
works.summary: Links literature notes, code-search artifacts, and manuscript claims through a Chain-of-Evidence workflow and four-part integrity audit. In 75 adapted ADRS runs, it reports strong score reproduction and reference identity checks, with human correction of flagged audit results. Majority-vote checks still miss documented exploits; MLE-bench medal results use repeated test-grader feedback rather than the official single-submission protocol.

works.name: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
works.summary: Google’s Gemini-based Co-Scientist generates, critiques and evolves research hypotheses through literature search and Elo-ranked agent debates. Expert-guided evaluations include selected AML drug and combination assays, liver-organoid tests and rediscovery of unpublished antimicrobial-resistance findings. Human screening and laboratory work remain central; several candidates failed, biological effects were context dependent, and automated Elo scores do not establish general scientific correctness.

works.name: Computational Discovery (Google Labs)
works.summary: Hosted scientific-coding tool built with ERA and AlphaEvolve, announced through Google’s trusted-tester program. The November 2026 update documents MCP integration for approved users alongside browser access. It offers a route to delegate computational investigations from compatible agents; access is gated, and the collection did not use the service. Published ERA research and generated application artifacts should be distinguished from availability or independent validation of this hosted product.

works.name: Empirical Research Assistance: An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software
works.summary: Uses LLM code rewriting and tree search to improve supplied scientific evaluation metrics, incorporating expert guidance, paper summaries, and recombined ideas. Experiments report gains in single-cell integration, retrospective forecasting, and other computational tasks. Results depend on task-specific scoring and data splits; forecasting comparisons use dated retrospective data, and implementation audits disclose failures and departures from some proposed methods.

works.name: Robin: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
works.summary: Combines literature retrieval, LLM-ranked therapeutic hypotheses and notebook data-analysis agents in a human-run experimental loop. The Nature study reports phagocytosis-enhancing candidates in cultured retinal cells, including primary cells from one donor. Experts supply protocols, physical experiments, preprocessing and analysis prompts; these in-vitro findings do not establish clinical effectiveness, and broad productivity gains are estimated rather than measured against a human research team.

works.name: NORA: A Harness-Engineered Autonomous Research Agent for End-to-End Spatial Data Science
works.summary: Orchestrates spatial research through domain skills, persistent files, separate reviewers, and human checkpoints. Three case studies demonstrate useful workflow assistance while recording substantial expert intervention and lower human ratings of rigor than LLM ratings. Ablations are qualitative. Generated reports retain unresolved validation issues, including an invalid fairness-bound argument and uncalibrated elevation uncertainty, so workflow completion should not be treated as verified scientific discovery.

works.name: PaperOrchestra
works.summary: Turns supplied ideas and experimental records into LaTeX manuscripts using planning, literature, plotting, writing, and refinement agents. On a benchmark reconstructed from 200 accepted papers, human reviewers prefer its drafts to two writing baselines. These comparisons assess manuscript quality; citation-identity checks and simulated acceptance do not validate underlying science, and generated figures and model-driven refinement require independent review.

works.name: LitPivot: Developing Well-Situated Research Ideas Through Dynamic Contextualization and Critique within the Literature Landscape
works.summary: Links proposal editing to changing literature: researchers select problem, contribution, or evaluation facets, inspect relevant paper clusters, and consider excerpt-backed critiques and revisions. A 17-participant study reports stronger expert-rated literature grounding, with a five-participant qualitative follow-up. Novelty benefits are self-reported; short HCI/NLP ideation tasks do not establish feasibility, successful experiments, or long-term research impact.

works.name: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
works.summary: Combines template-based and template-free agents for research ideas, experiments, manuscripts, and automated review. The Nature paper consolidates earlier AI Scientist reports and adds analyses; its workshop campaign overlaps v2. One selected manuscript received acceptance-level reviews before withdrawal. Human selection, code and data errors, and model-based evaluation constrain claims of independent scientific validation.

works.name: OpenScientist: evaluating an open agentic AI co-scientist to accelerate biomedical discovery
works.summary: Evaluates an open hypothesis-testing agent on four featured biomedical case studies and three supplementary cases, combining data analysis, literature retrieval, and reports. Expert review identifies useful results alongside preprocessing mistakes, statistical weaknesses, and incomplete rejection on randomized controls. Selected cases and human prompt/data refinement limit generalization; estimated time savings are not a controlled productivity comparison.

works.name: RINoBench
works.summary: Tests novelty judgments on 1,381 ideas extracted by an LLM from ICLR submissions, paired with binned reviewer scores and model-synthesized explanations. Nine metrics assess score agreement and justifications against supplied related-work abstracts. Models produce plausible explanations while poorly matching novelty ratings. These are subjective, filtered machine-learning review labels, with further LLM processing and grading; they do not measure universal novelty or scientific validity.

works.name: EvoScientist: Towards Multi-Agent Evolving AI Scientists for End-to-End Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Coordinates a researcher, engineer and evolution manager that turn prior idea reviews and execution trajectories into retrievable ideation and experimentation memories. On 30 curated AI queries, it reports stronger judged ideas and higher mean code-execution success after memory updates. Human comparisons cover four baselines; selected conference-track acceptances are case evidence, and execution success does not establish scientific correctness or cross-domain autonomous discovery.

works.name: MOOSE-Star: Unlocking Tractable Training for Scientific Discovery by Breaking the Complexity Barrier
works.summary: Trains hypothesis generation through decomposed discovery subtasks, motivation-guided hierarchical retrieval, and bounded composition. TOMATO-Star supplies paper-derived supervision; evaluations measure retrieval and LLM-scored reconstruction of held-out hypotheses. The best-case complexity reduction relies on compositional and routing assumptions, and the study does not prospectively validate new discoveries.

works.name: FIRE-Bench
works.summary: Asks research agents to rediscover published empirical findings from high-level questions while withholding original procedures and conclusions. Research-problem trees define tasks; LLM claim extraction and entailment generate reference-aligned precision, recall and F1. Human checks cover extraction on a subset, rather than end-to-end scientific validity. Valid alternative findings can be penalized, and inspected software inventories differ from the paper’s evaluated tasks.

works.name: AutoIllustrate
works.summary: Converts a method description into an editable draw.io diagram, then optionally applies an image-generation restyling pass. The public command-line workflow includes figure generation and visual auditing and was used with Agentic Scientist. Retaining the vector source supports manual correction, but generated visual polish should not be taken as evidence of methodological fidelity.

works.name: Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap
works.summary: Examines computational research agents through autonomy, evaluation, released artifacts, human intervention, novelty checks, and result-selection disclosure. Its coded corpus distinguishes runnable code from evidence that supports scientific claims. The conclusions are bounded by the screened AI/ML systems and coding rules, rather than a census of all scientific domains.

works.name: OpenResearch
works.summary: A local research workspace and harness from alphaXiv that connects coding agents to literature discovery, experiment execution, and artifact inspection. It records experiments in a local database and supports multiple compute backends. The repository documents a usable product; these capabilities are project claims rather than an independently established discovery benchmark.

works.name: PaperBanana
works.summary: Uses retrieval, planning, styling, visualization, and critique agents to generate academic diagrams and plots from scientific content. Its repository includes execution interfaces and a benchmark of reference illustrations. It is a useful study of iterative visual communication, with semantic accuracy and faithful representation of experimental data still requiring inspection beyond aesthetic judgments.

works.name: AInsteinBench
works.summary: Evaluates scientific software development with 244 tasks from maintainer pull requests and synthesized feature-completion exercises across six research codebases. Containerized tests assess patches, while expert review and case studies examine scientific invariants and test defects. This measures repository implementation under specified tests; passing does not establish correctness beyond their coverage or autonomous hypothesis selection.

works.name: FrontierScience
works.summary: Assesses expert-level physics, chemistry, and biology reasoning using Olympiad and Research splits. The released gold sets contain 100 short-answer questions and 60 research subtasks, with model grading against answers or rubrics. These constrained, expert-authored tasks probe scientific reasoning; the creators explicitly distinguish them from the broader work of producing new discoveries.

works.name: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
works.summary: Coordinates parallel literature and data-analysis agents through a structured world model to produce source-linked discovery reports from human-curated datasets. Seven case studies include reproduced findings and new hypotheses, with human reanalysis and external validation. Experts supported79.4% of102 sampled statements, with lower interpretation accuracy; reported months of saved work are collaborator estimates, and one final discovery report involved manual curation.

works.name: A Survey of AI Scientists
works.summary: Synthesizes AI-scientist systems through six stages covering literature, ideas, preparation, execution, writing, and paper generation. The revised survey traces the shift from individual components to integrated workflows and discusses robustness and governance. Its stage-based organization is useful for comparing coverage, but does not make unlike evaluation settings directly comparable.

works.name: From AI for Science to Agentic Science: A Survey on Autonomous Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Organizes agentic science across life sciences, chemistry, materials, and physics, connecting capability, workflow, and domain perspectives. It provides a useful map of hypothesis generation, experimentation, analysis, and refinement. As a survey, its taxonomy helps navigate reported systems rather than independently reproducing their discovery or autonomy claims.

works.name: The Virtual Lab of AI agents designs new SARS-CoV-2 nanobodies
works.summary: Organizes a principal-investigator agent and scientific specialists into meetings with high-level human guidance. The agents develop a computational nanobody-design workflow, with selected designs tested experimentally. This demonstrates a specific human-AI research collaboration; human laboratory work and biological validation are central parts of the evidence.

works.name: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
works.summary: Recruits researchers to execute randomly assigned human- or model-generated NLP ideas, then obtains blinded reviews of the resulting projects. AI proposals show larger declines from ideation ratings, but final project-level differences are not statistically conclusive. Attrition, implementation changes, and differences between review stages qualify interpretation; the study demonstrates why proposal ratings alone are weak proxies for completed research quality.

works.name: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
works.summary: Evolves candidate programs using language-model edits and feedback from executable evaluators. Applications include mathematical constructions, algorithm discovery, and infrastructure optimization. The white paper illustrates breadth when a reliable scoring procedure exists; reported improvements are tied to those tasks and do not imply autonomous formulation of every scientific objective.

works.name: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
works.summary: Combines retrieval-guided planning and executable code with an environment of biomedical tools, software, and databases. Evaluations span heterogeneous tasks, multimodal data analysis, and experimental protocol design. The reported breadth supports biomedical research assistance; benchmark performance and protocol case studies should not be treated as general clinical validation.

works.name: ScienceBoard
works.summary: A desktop environment and 169-task benchmark for scientific software use across six domains. Agents act through GUI or command-line interfaces using screenshots, accessibility trees or marked images; application-state and output checks determine completion. Experiments expose grounding, software-knowledge and interface-selection difficulties, with improvements from hybrid interfaces and separated planning/grounding. These results concern bounded digital workflows; revised tables and older headline prose report different aggregate rates.

works.name: MOOSE-Chem2: Exploring LLM Limits in Fine-Grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery via Hierarchical Search
works.summary: Expands coarse research directions into increasingly detailed hypotheses through hierarchical search, comparing different language-model scoring ensembles. Evaluation uses expert-annotated fine-grained hypotheses from recent literature. The study tests alignment with known hypotheses and model-defined rewards; a detailed, high-scoring proposal still needs independent checks and experimental testing.

works.name: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation
works.summary: Combines literature/code analysis, concept-to-implementation mapping, iterative advisor-guided experiments, and hierarchical manuscript drafting. Scientist-Bench evaluates guided and reference-only ML research tasks using execution checks and LLM rubric/pairwise judgments. Reported completion differs from correctness, reviewer preferences vary substantially, and benchmark prompts can expose target-method details; the study does not independently establish human-level scientific quality.

works.name: AI Idea Bench 2025
works.summary: Evaluates AI research idea generation using 3,495 target papers and their motivating references. Its protocol compares generated ideas with paper content and reference-based judgments, including novelty and feasibility assessments. Historical alignment provides a repeatable proxy for ideation quality, but resemblance to published work cannot establish prospective novelty, successful execution, or future scientific impact.

works.name: MLRC-Bench
works.summary: Adapts seven ML competitions into repository-level research tasks with protected evaluators and held-out testing. It measures improvement relative to baseline and top human solutions, and contrasts executed performance with LLM assessments of idea quality. Results are best-of-eight attempts; pass@k counts a 5% closure of the human-performance gap. Competition gains provide objective task evidence, while research novelty and transfer beyond these seven tasks require separate evaluation.

works.name: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
works.summary: Replaces code templates with staged agentic tree search, replication nodes, and visual feedback for experiments and manuscripts. Humans selected three ideas and the best outputs from multiple autonomous runs for workshop review; one passed and was withdrawn as agreed. Internal audits document train/test overlap, misdescribed methods, and claimed experiments absent from successful code, so acceptance is bounded evidence of workshop-level manuscript quality.

works.name: PaperBench
works.summary: Measures reconstruction of 20 ML papers from scratch using author-approved rubrics, clean-environment execution, and an LLM grader. Scores combine partial credit for code, execution, and result matching; they are not the fraction of papers fully reproduced. Human comparisons cover a small selected subset with different selection and time budgets. The cheaper Code-Dev variant omits execution and result verification.

works.name: SciReplicate-Bench
works.summary: Assesses algorithm comprehension and implementation through 100 tasks extracted from 36 NLP papers published in 2024. Evaluation combines executable tests, reasoning-graph comparison, and repository dependency or API measures. Its scope is reproducing selected algorithmic components from papers; passing those tasks does not imply that every experiment or headline paper result was replicated.

works.name: AgentRxiv: Towards Collaborative Autonomous Research
works.summary: Adds a searchable shared report archive to Agent Laboratory so sequential or parallel research agents can reuse earlier findings. Prompting-search experiments improve best-so-far MATH-500 accuracy and show mixed transfer to other QA benchmarks. The target test set guides repeated search, parallel runs use more resources, and humans manually verify code and outputs because agents can fabricate results or remove essential method logic.

works.name: BixBench
works.summary: Evaluates bioinformatics agents on 61 expert-curated analysis scenarios with 205 associated questions. Agents explore supplied data and run notebook analyses; open responses are graded against reference answers, with separate multiple-choice experiments. The tested models reach about 21% open-answer accuracy. Shared-scenario questions and model-based judging limit interpretation, and prepared analysis success does not validate new biological mechanisms or experimental discoveries.

works.name: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
works.summary: Assists a human-supplied research idea through literature review, iterative ML coding, and report drafting, with optional feedback checkpoints. Small human studies find useful outputs but substantially lower paper-quality scores than automated reviewers; co-pilot gains concentrate in quality and presentation. Separate MLE-bench tests evaluate the solver component, while reported cost savings compare different workflow settings rather than matched scientific outcomes.

works.name: AIDE
works.summary: Searches executable ML solutions through draft, debug, and improvement branches scored by a supplied metric. Author Kaggle experiments and separately reported MLE-Bench/RE-Bench evaluations support bounded engineering utility. Historical leaderboard comparisons use differing holdouts and retain contamination risks; task-level labels in one table conflict with its definition. Results depend on model, budget, evaluator, and search space, and do not establish autonomous selection of scientific questions.

works.name: OpenEvolve
works.summary: An open community implementation inspired by AlphaEvolve that evolves programs using language models, evaluator feedback, and population-based search. It includes examples for mathematical optimization, scientific computing, and kernel improvement. The repository is independently maintained rather than Google's original system, and its reported improvements should be checked against the corresponding evaluator and hardware conditions.

works.name: R&D-Agent
works.summary: A modular framework for autonomous machine-learning engineering that separates idea search from implementation and feedback. Its tested agent combines adaptive parallel exploration, structured hypothesis generation, collaborative memory, sampled-data debugging and standardized solution selection. MLE-Bench experiments report competition-medal gains with matched ML-Master reruns and selected-subset ablations. The evidence concerns bounded data-science optimization, with historical comparisons subject to differing models, hardware and budgets.

works.name: ShinkaEvolve
works.summary: Evolves programs against human-defined executable objectives using island archives, language-model mutations, novelty rejection, and adaptive model selection. Experiments cover circle packing, AIME scaffolds, ALE-Bench solutions, and MoE load balancing. Reported gains are task-dependent: exact circle-packing validation requires postprocessing, and the AIME 2025 scaffold trails majority voting. Open code supports local or cluster evaluation.

works.name: ToolUniverse
works.summary: Provides a common interface for scientific tools, datasets, models, and APIs so language-model agents can discover and invoke external capabilities. The public project offers a Python SDK and agent integrations. It supplies infrastructure for building scientific assistants; available tool connectors do not by themselves establish reliable tool selection, valid analyses, or experimental reproducibility.

works.name: Autonomous LLM-driven research from data to human-verifiable research papers
works.summary: Guides agents from annotated data through hypotheses, analysis code, and manuscripts while linking numeric results back to producing code. Repeated case studies show fewer major errors for simple tasks, limited novelty, and failures on complex data or goals that require human review. The evaluated workflow includes prepared metadata and step approvals; traceability supports verification without establishing scientific correctness.

works.name: RE-Bench
works.summary: Compares agents with human experts on seven open-ended machine-learning research engineering environments, including optimization tasks with executable scoring functions. Its human-attempt data and multiple time budgets make resource assumptions visible. Results concern bounded AI research engineering, and rankings can change with time allowance; they do not establish general scientific autonomy.

works.name: CycleResearcher: Improving Automated Research via Automated Review
works.summary: Trains research-writing and reviewing models through supervised learning and iterative preference optimization. Main evaluations score manuscripts whose experimental results are deliberately fabricated, so simulated acceptance measures writing and reviewer alignment. Human reviewers rate selected outputs below typical submissions. A separate executed appendix example uses an external coding agent, but contains numerical and interpretation errors that limit claims of validated discovery.

works.name: MLE-bench
works.summary: Packages 75 Kaggle competitions to assess dataset preparation, model training, and iterative experimentation, with historical leaderboard thresholds as reference points. Useful for engineering-focused research agents and resource-scaling studies. A competition medal measures predictive performance under a particular setup; it is not evidence of novel hypotheses or scientific validity beyond that task.

works.name: MOOSE-Chem: Large Language Models for Rediscovering Unseen Chemistry Scientific Hypotheses
works.summary: MOOSE-Chem retrieves paper inspirations and evolves chemistry hypotheses through LLM mutation, critique and recombination. On 51 retrospectively decomposed papers it recovers parts of known innovations, but evaluation seeds the literature corpus with the true inspirations and selects candidates using answer-aware similarity scores. Expert ratings are lower than automatic scores, ranking remains weak, and proposed chemistry is not experimentally validated.

works.name: ScienceAgentBench
works.summary: A 102-task benchmark for generating executable Python programs that process, analyze and visualize scientific data across four disciplines. Expert validation, dataset modifications, task-specific outcome checks and human process rubrics support evaluation. Comparisons of prompting, self-debug and OpenHands show that successful execution can still produce scientifically incorrect results. Reported headline success uses the best of three attempts; tasks and source materials cover a bounded portion of scientific workflows.

works.name: Scideator: Human-LLM Compound System for Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation
works.summary: Extracts purpose, mechanism, and evaluation facets from papers so researchers can recombine ideas and inspect related work for novelty. A 22-person CS study reports greater perceived creativity support than a bundled baseline; separate ablations test retrieval and classification. Novelty confidence and several idea-quality ratings do not improve, and neither the study nor its retrieval-based labels validate completed scientific results.

works.name: CORE-Bench
works.summary: A computational-reproducibility benchmark with 270 tasks formed by three assistance levels over 90 scientific code packages. Agents recover selected outputs from known reproducible CodeOcean capsules, ranging from reading supplied results to installing dependencies and executing code. Original AutoGPT and CORE-Agent experiments expose environment and result-retrieval failures. The task construction tests selected output recovery, and a distinct 2026 companion revises shortcut-prone or incorrectly graded tasks.

works.name: PaperQA2
works.summary: Searches papers iteratively, summarizes and reranks evidence, traverses citations, and produces cited answers. LitQA2 evaluation finds higher answer precision than human annotators, with comparable overall accuracy. WikiCrow and ContraCrow extend the approach to summaries and contradiction screening; human agreement depends on the evidence and reasoning shown. The evaluated configuration and accessible full-text corpus differ from a default open-package installation.

works.name: SciAgents: Automating Scientific Discovery Through Bioinspired Multi-Agent Intelligent Graph Reasoning
works.summary: SciAgents uses knowledge-graph paths and specialized LLM agents to generate, expand and critique biologically inspired materials proposals. A literature-search assistant assigns novelty and feasibility scores to illustrative examples. Reported mechanical, optical and energy improvements are predictions; the study does not synthesize materials, execute the proposed simulations or independently establish superiority over human research.

works.name: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
works.summary: Compares expert-written NLP prompting proposals with selected agent-generated proposals in blinded reviews involving 104 researchers. AI proposals receive higher novelty ratings across several analyses; lower feasibility estimates are not statistically conclusive. Limited idea diversity, unreliable automatic ranking, and unfaithful execution-agent implementations constrain interpretation. The study measures perceived proposal quality rather than demonstrated scientific outcomes.

works.name: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Uses human-prepared ML experiment templates, literature-assisted ideation, Aider code edits, experiment logs, and LaTeX generation to produce papers and automated reviews. Three small computational task families show substantial execution and writing attrition; reported acceptance thresholds come from its own reviewer. The paper documents metric errors, implementation mistakes, data leakage, hallucinated details, and unsafe execution behavior requiring human checks.

works.name: SciCode
works.summary: Uses 80 scientist-authored research coding problems, decomposed into 338 subproblems across 16 subfields, to test scientific knowledge and executable implementation. Report main-problem and subproblem accuracy separately, including whether background information was supplied. This assesses specified computational tasks; the later SciCode-Verified audit also makes benchmark version and test defects relevant to comparisons.

works.name: LAB-Bench
works.summary: Collects 2,457 multiple-choice tasks spanning literature, figures, tables, databases, protocols and biological sequences. Original baselines compare tool-free language models with experts allowed web and research tools, so the human gap is not a matched agent comparison. Small free-response checks expose distractor-based guessing. These bounded questions do not establish laboratory execution, complete biological research, or novel experimental validation.

works.name: DiscoveryBench
works.summary: Tests hypothesis discovery from supplied datasets, metadata, and natural-language goals using 264 literature-derived tasks across six domains, plus 903 synthetic tasks. Facet-based evaluation separates aspects of a proposed finding. The target is recovering supported relationships within provided data, with synthetic and real tasks reported separately, rather than discovering unrestricted new scientific knowledge.

works.name: BioDiscoveryAgent: An AI Agent for Designing Genetic Perturbation Experiments
works.summary: Uses an LLM to select genetic perturbation batches, incorporate observed phenotypes, and optionally retrieve literature, search gene databases, or critique selections. Retrospective replay across six single-gene screens and one paired-gene screen measures hit discovery against optimization and random baselines. Gains depend on dataset, model, and budget; added tools can hurt stronger models, and the study does not establish prospective autonomous biological discovery.

works.name: ChemCrow: Augmenting large language models with chemistry tools
works.summary: ChemCrow equips GPT-4 with chemistry tools for retrieval, molecular analysis, synthesis planning and robotic execution. It synthesized four known compounds and helped a human-guided workflow identify a new chromophore, whose absorption differed by 33 nm from the target. Expert evaluations favour factuality over tool-free GPT-4, but reasoning failures persist; laboratory oversight and proprietary services remain necessary, and the public release includes only 12 of 18 tools.

works.name: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
works.summary: ResearchAgent combines citation-linked paper abstracts, retrieved entities and LLM reviewers to draft and iteratively refine research problems, methods and experiment plans. Human and model evaluations favour the full GPT-4 system over simpler variants, while weaker backbones benefit inconsistently. Evidence concerns proposal ratings; the system does not execute experiments, and entity-linking noise and reviewer agreement limit claims of scientific validity.

works.name: Docling
works.summary: Converts documents into structured representations using page-layout analysis, table reconstruction, optional OCR, and typed assembly. Its technical report benchmarks runtime on five documents totaling 225 pages with OCR disabled, rather than establishing general extraction accuracy. Published examples omit figure text and break a cross-column paragraph; Markdown repeats spanning headers while JSON retains spans. Current software capabilities should be checked separately from this historical report.

works.name: MLAgentBench
works.summary: An executable benchmark of 13 machine-learning experimentation tasks with starter code, data and automatic evaluators. A ReAct-derived agent reads, edits and runs experiments while maintaining plans and fact-check statements. Eight-trial experiments across seven backbones show strong task dependence, with better results on established datasets than several newer challenges. The benchmark measures bounded optimization tasks; qualitative traces expose persistent planning, interpretation and submission errors despite explicit checking prompts.

works.name: OpenScholar
works.summary: A scientific-literature synthesis system combining specialized retrieval, reranking, citation-linked generation and iterative feedback. The author-linked preprint evaluates answer quality, attribution and expert preference across several disciplines, while documenting persistent factuality and retrieval limitations. Human preference chiefly reflects coverage and presentation, rather than independently verified correctness. The later Nature publication is linked by the authors, but its main text and supplements remain unread in this audit.

works.name: STORM / Co-STORM
works.summary: STORM develops cited articles through perspective-guided questions, web-grounded conversations, and outline refinement. Its Co-STORM companion lets users steer simulated-expert discussions and organizes findings in a shared mind map. Evaluations support aspects of organization and user preference; small human studies and model-based grading do not establish objective learning gains, complete factual accuracy, or publication-ready scientific reporting.

works.name: Coscientist: Autonomous chemical research with large language models
works.summary: Coscientist connects GPT-4 planning, web and documentation search, code execution and laboratory APIs. It executes known coupling reactions and bounded instrument tasks, with researcher-prepared resources, manual plate movement and occasional guidance. Reaction-optimization results use previously collected datasets rather than a live laboratory loop. Only a simplified implementation is released, and the demonstrations do not establish autonomous novel chemical discovery.

works.name: FunSearch: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
works.summary: Pairs a language model with an evaluator and an evolving database of programs, searching for code that constructs strong solutions. The paper reports new cap-set constructions and improved bin-packing heuristics. Its successes depend on explicit evaluators and problem specifications, making the verification mechanism central to its scientific relevance.

works.name: GPT Researcher
works.summary: A configurable research agent that decomposes questions, gathers evidence from web or local sources, and assembles cited reports. It exposes a package, interfaces, and multi-agent or recursive research workflows. It is useful as a general research component, but its project-level claims should not be confused with scientific novelty or independently validated literature-review completeness.

works.name: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
works.summary: SciMON retrieves semantic, graph and citation-based inspirations to generate scientific idea sentences, then revises suggestions that resemble prior work. Expert studies find improvements over baseline models, but NLP ideas remain substantially less novel and technically detailed than source papers. Evaluations use extracted problem contexts and seed terms; novelty gains are conditional on selected revisions, without executing the proposed research.

works.name: ASReview LAB
works.summary: Uses active learning to prioritize records during systematic literature screening while preserving human inclusion decisions. It provides a screening interface, simulation tools, label management, and exportable review state. This is a complementary evidence-selection tool rather than a generative scientist; screening completeness depends on the review protocol, labels, and stopping decision.

works.name: The Automation of Science (Robot Scientist Adam)
works.summary: Combines hypothesis generation, automated laboratory experiments, and a logical record of the research process to study yeast functional genomics. The authors report manual confirmation of Adam's conclusions. This pre-LLM example grounds modern autonomy discussions in a closed experimental loop and explicit provenance within a constrained biological problem.

records.name: Adaptive Experimentation Can Hide Model Error: Detection Limits and Falsification Budget
records.summary: Bounds model-adequacy detection in stationary, finite-action/outcome settings using the experimenter’s sampling distribution. Separates absent acquisition evidence from a detector’s failure to capture available signal. An expansion-relative diagnostic motivates reserving actions for falsification. Empirical evidence is mixed: the primary comparison fails detection eligibility, revisions depend on horizon, and measured-data replay retains fit-derived labels. Small selected LLM pilots and incomplete campaigns do not establish general scientific-reasoning gains.

records.name: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
records.summary: Combines paper-derived skills and parallel hypothesis investigations to deliver drug-discovery candidates. Evaluations cover 121 decision questions, three LLM-graded process tasks, and three selected studies followed by human assays. LpxH activity/binding and cytokine-signaling inhibition do not confirm the proposed binding site, covalency, or JAK1 selectivity. An anonymized target study and differing tool/skill access limit scrutiny and component attribution; learning from experimental outcomes remains future work.

records.name: SwarmEvolve benchmark
records.summary: Combines 16 AlphaEvolve-derived mathematical construction problems with five numerical-science tasks scored by deterministic evaluators against reference solutions. Author comparisons use three seeds and one-hour budgets on one GPU with eight CPU evaluation cores. The release documents task specifications, initial programs, evaluators, and baseline scripts; evaluator quality and fixed tasks bound the conclusions, and the core proposed search implementation is still planned.

records.name: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
records.summary: Accelerates evolutionary program search with batched latent agents, KV-cache communication, and hidden-state diversity filtering. Across 21 numerical tasks it evaluates more programs per hour than three text-based frameworks. Ablations show early search benefits, while zero-agent variants approach similar final scores. Improvements over historical AlphaEvolve constructions do not establish new global records, and fixed numerical evaluations provide limited evidence of broader scientific generalization.

records.name: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
records.summary: Coordinates dataset discovery, quality screening, and code-based transformation for scientific RAG and instruction tuning. Biomedical and chemistry benchmarks support useful corpus construction, with smaller gains for chemistry retrieval than fine-tuning. Efficiency comparisons use measured pipeline runtime against expert time estimates. Reported overlap controls reduce contamination risk, while derived sources, dataset-level quality judgments, and corpus composition limit claims of verified scientific knowledge or autonomous discovery.

records.name: CLEAR: Structured Specifications for Controllable Long-Horizon ML Research Engineering
records.summary: Converts papers and task descriptions into structured execution specifications, then uses a planner, coding workers, and localized repairs to construct ML pipelines. Evaluation covers PaperBench and MLE-Bench Lite; a matched-backbone specification ablation supports the intermediate representation. Other comparisons change model backbones as well as orchestration, limiting causal claims about heterogeneous routing. The optional human specification checkpoint was not used in reported runs.

records.name: FrontierPhysics
records.summary: A benchmark of 56 physics research tasks designed by 42 physicists from their own projects. Agents select methods, produce numerical artifacts and write manuscripts, assessed through deterministic verifiers and expert-authored rubrics applied by a reviewing agent. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, the best passes 46 of 168 trials. Expert trajectory audits expose reasoning and intuition failures, alongside residual evaluation errors; detailed diagnoses apply to the audited model–harness cohort.
records.status: Reviewed v1 sections 2–3: results use v0.1 and a ten-hour rollout cap. An author-maintained fork provides source documentation, but its referenced canonical repository did not resolve publicly during inspection; availability of the complete evaluated 56-task package was not established. No tasks or trajectories were downloaded or executed.

records.name: A semi-autonomous multi-agent pipeline for high-energy astrophysics research with enforced provenance and verifiable self-extension
records.summary: Builds reusable astronomy tools behind deterministic checks and cross-model review, while requiring reported numbers to occur in recorded outputs or carry paper locators. On a planted-defect benchmark, the combined checks stop 64 of 65 defects but reject 40 of 69 correct controls. IXPE studies include qualified reproduction and null results. Provenance does not ensure scientific correctness; statistical and source-mixing errors survive the checks.

records.name: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
records.summary: Packages expert defect-calculation protocols as reusable prompts for VASP setup, convergence checks, finite-size corrections, formation energies, and thermodynamic analysis. A BaCd2P2 demonstration covers seven defect species but requires researcher intervention on restart diagnosis, directory mapping, and substitution of a custom solver. The run informed prompt refinement; it does not establish held-out reliability or detailed defect-physics validation. Reference scripts and calculation data are linked.

records.name: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?
records.summary: Compares persistent and reset research agents on matched streams across nine ML task families. Persistent state improves early search efficiency, largely through faster or stronger initialization; only one agent shows a substantial aggregate final-performance gain. Matched insight cards do not consistently beat shuffled cards. Short fixed streams, mostly single paired runs, and bundled code–context retention limit claims about scientific learning across tasks.
records.status: Reviewed v1, sections 3–6 and memory/failure appendices. Models remain fixed; streams contain three to five tasks, usually with 30-minute budgets. The reproducibility statement schedules code release for a camera-ready version; public benchmark code was not established.

records.name: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness
records.summary: Demonstrates revised display-control software, spectral feedback, and response-model refinement in one optical see-through color-matching setup. An acknowledged RGB-hold interface passes 12 live control checks. Feedback improves five targets; a separate model revision helps seven of nine paired contexts, with two regressions. The error bound assumes uniform model accuracy and global optimization, neither established by sampled prediction scores; cross-goal transfer and general hardware redesign remain untested.
records.status: Reviewed v1 sections 4–7 and the source tree/README at 255a2f896040. The release covers device-control and acquisition software, not verified end-to-end research-agent orchestration. Observed measurements, fitted models, calibration, and vendor SDKs are excluded. No software or hardware was executed here.

records.name: Verifier strength does not buy discovery quality: a pre-registered two-domain test of LLM-based automated research, with post-hoc evidence pointing to proposer-pool composition
records.summary: Re-gates fixed LLM and random proposal pools through three verifier tiers in scheduling and simulated edge offloading. Under author-reported frozen criteria, stricter filtering does not produce the predicted held-out ordering. Weak and standard gates usually select identical candidates. Exploratory pool merging helps only scheduling and also doubles proposal count. One 0.5B proposer, overlapping source instances, weak tier separation, and an unreachable strict-order criterion limit generalization.
records.status: Reviewed v1, sections 3–7. The linked Zenodo artifact record is restricted and exposes no public files; its protocols and ledgers were not independently audited. The manuscript’s journal-template heading was not treated as a publication record.

records.name: Are LLM Research Agents Reliable Judges of Predictability? Evidence from Planted-Signal Worlds
