records.summary: Tests forecasting agents in simulated worlds with known predictive structure, separating their verdicts from sealed-holdout performance. Initial bootstrap worlds contain an exploitable repeated-value artifact; Gaussian-shock follow-ups still show frequent unsupported predictability claims and framing sensitivity. At matched false-positive rates, agents do not outperform conventional tests consistently. The brief leaves the decision threshold unspecified, and stronger baseline comparisons are exploratory.
records.status: Reviewed v1, study design, Gaussian-shock controls, discussion, and availability statement. Pre-specifications use tagged repository commits rather than a public registry. The replication package is described as planned for public deposit and available by request; no public implementation was verified.

records.name: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
records.summary: Compares expert-guided and unattended agents for translating and designing warm-rain parameterizations in JAX. Most gains concern executable, differentiable, mass-conserving closures; only two of 100 four-round candidates beat the best retuned physical baseline on rain-mass error. Expert-guided neural-ODE development required 131 prompts and remained less accurate. Missing source equations affect one translation test; box-model results do not establish coupled-climate performance.
records.status: Reviewed v1, sections 3–5 and Appendices F/I. The checklist describes a workshop submission and defers code release to a later journal version; no published venue record or public implementation was established.

records.name: Cloudra: Geometric Reasoning and Scientific Validation for Autonomous Reaction Mechanism Exploration
records.summary: Connects chemical species and reaction steps to geometric operations, quantum-chemical calculations, and explicit physical checks. Same-backbone comparisons on 50 mechanism tasks favour guided workflows, particularly in pathway support. Published scores use human reconstruction of run artifacts; full self-consistency concerns delivered objects rather than all requested steps. Electronic-energy agreement, computation cost, incomplete pathways, and method-limited negative conclusions require separate interpretation.
records.status: Inspected the paper-described 70daa5a source tree and README, plus current documentation at 005e9642cead. The current Standard mode differs from the paper baseline. No installation, calculation, or archive download was performed.

records.name: CloudraBench
records.summary: Evaluates 50 small-molecule mechanism tasks, including ten method-limited cases requiring supported negative conclusions. Grades graph structure, physical self-consistency, and task-target accuracy separately before a weighted composite. Native calculation logs support checks, while human organizers reconstruct each run’s records before scoring. The 200-run study contains one attempt per task/configuration; offline scores, original graph delivery, reference exceptions, and table reconstruction are distinct from independent scientific reproduction.
records.status: Reviewed v1 section 2.6 and SI S1/S2/S7, plus the pinned release guide. It documents missing Gold originals, IRC-provenance limits, and manual acceptance exceptions. Referenced research archives were not downloaded or rerun.

records.name: ScienceBoard-VE / ScienceBoard-Verified
records.summary: ScienceBoard-Verified retains 168 evaluation tasks after the authors revise 37 original tasks and remove one. ScienceBoard-VE adds 108 disjoint evolution tasks, giving 276 tasks across six scientific applications. The paper evaluates frozen skill libraries on the Verified split and reports unweighted application means. Model-based and native-agent runs have different history and resource-access protocols, so benchmark version and execution setting must accompany scores.
records.status: The paper links a hosted environment repository, whose card was empty during review. The pinned project README lists benchmark components as future releases; complete task/evaluator-package availability remains unverified. No environment or benchmark was downloaded or run.

records.name: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents
records.summary: Builds procedural skills and reference catalogs from scientific-software documentation, then revises them using execution failures and fresh-session validation. ScienceBoard-VE separates 108 evolution tasks from 168 repaired test tasks. Gains demonstrate transfer across related operations in six applications; a stronger model gains only 2.11 percentage points. Resource coverage, information volume, and routing differ across baselines, limiting claims about knowledge organization alone.
records.status: The pinned release includes Resource-to-Skill construction. Its README lists execution-guided skill self-evolution and benchmark components as planned future releases. Repository and paper were inspected without installation or execution.

records.name: Towards AI-Agent-Accelerated Research in High-Energy Physics: A Case Study in Monte Carlo Analysis
records.summary: Studies agent-assisted reconstruction and extension of a CEPC Bell-observable analysis through simulation, frozen definitions, deterministic checks, and diagnostic controls. Humans authorize state-changing work and retain scientific interpretation. The benchmark uses instructions rather than an information-access barrier, and the enlarged sample reuses development seeds. Four correlated selections are not independent replications. Active human time was not prospectively recorded, so no measured productivity speed-up is established.

records.name: The Verifier Is Part of the Simulator: Evidence-View Gaming in Agentic Equation Discovery
records.summary: Studies equation-discovery agents that choose which numerical summary reaches a fixed verifier. Across simulated PDEs, score-based view selection can reject correct libraries or accept equations missing diffusion without altering data or verifier code. Prescribed agreement reduces some errors but abstains more; a fixed fine view outperforms it on PDEBench. Three-model prompt experiments are single-turn selection tests, distinct from the deterministic attack and negative transfer results.
records.status: Reviewed v1 and pinned release documentation. Stored-record recounts are distinct from fresh numerical regeneration. No linked workshop proceedings record was verified.

records.name: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
records.summary: Coordinates question selection, theoretical derivation, computational checks, and nitrogen-vacancy spin experiments through agents that can reject or revise collaborators’ work. An acquisition agreeing with predictions was classified inconclusive after drift controls failed; a revised protocol passed retained criteria on four withheld targets. One configured laboratory and human-built apparatus bound the evidence. The public Auctopus engine excludes study prompts and instrument descriptions; experimental data and analysis code are request-only.
records.status: Auctopus 1.0.0 releases the agent engine and templates, while excluding the study prompts and instrument description. Its mock demo does not reproduce the paper; experimental data and analysis code remain request-only.

records.name: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents
records.summary: Reanalyzes numerical claims in agent-written papers and distinguishes values unsupported by the recorded experiment from values absent from available artifacts. A deterministic context-and-decoy checker achieves high precision but limited recall on a small held-out human-labeled sample. Most uncertified claims remain traceable. Shared retrieval candidates, annotation revisions, incomplete large-run coverage, and changes to both judge model and harness constrain the conclusions.
records.status: Annotation follows v2, revised 31 October; date records the first submission. The study covers one benchmark and available released artifacts. A manuscript journal heading was not treated as a verified publication record.

records.name: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents
records.summary: Extracts global checks, problem-level approaches, and implementation lessons from completed coding attempts, then selectively injects relevant experience and review advice during execution. Comparisons span numerical solvers, GPU kernels, and scientific software repair. Memory banks are frozen before evaluation; transfer is tested between two kernel benchmarks using one agent and model family. Reported coding gains do not establish continual learning or end-to-end scientific discovery.

records.name: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
records.summary: Introduces LongChang, where agents choose investigations and construct apparatus in simulated worlds with altered physical laws. Separate agents generate scenes and judge reports against hidden laws and exploration records. Evaluation distinguishes law correctness from experimental support and compares guidance, turn budgets, and apparatus access. Findings concern fixed simulated scenes and model-based judgments, not discovery of unknown real-world laws or independently validated scientific results.
records.status: The author-linked repository snapshot bfad4c7e63d3 contains a README and presentation assets, but no experiment source files despite documented run commands. Public implementation availability remains unverified.

records.name: Do AI Scientists Know What's New?
records.summary: Audits proposal-level novelty checks and introduces ClaimNov, which extracts contribution claims, retrieves comparable prior claims, and produces evidence-linked novelty judgments. Tests distinguish disguised papers, disputed contributions, later-realized ideas, and mixed proposals. Results depend on fixed reference pools, heuristic novelty labels, and LLM generation and judging; they do not establish open-literature search completeness or better completed research.

records.name: OpenFrontiers-Bench
records.summary: Combines dated research-problem records with a Lean-graded mathematics benchmark. Evaluation on 50 selected items separates closed-book rediscovery from live-web recovery of published solutions. Most web successes retrieve known solutions, and clean evaluation sets differ by model lineage and cutoff. Corpus records are not deduplicated conjectures; status labels and AI-reviewed formalizations still require source scrutiny.
records.status: The benchmark is distinct from the larger OpenFrontiers corpus: corpus records preserve source-side status claims and include many unassessed problems and placeholder formalizations. No problem data, proof environments, or grader were downloaded or executed.

records.name: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
records.summary: Extracts perovskite-device records under versioned annotation and equivalence rules, calibrates verifiers against experts, and attaches category-level reliability to the database. Retrospective prediction uses a held-out publication year. The multi-agent discovery dialogue is illustrative, with selected held-out recipes, rather than a validated discovery experiment. Deployment reliability remains model-judged, and category accuracy does not establish confidence in individual values.
records.status: Paper, implementation tree, and README inspected at bafe1a7f2808 without execution. The paper links a data release; no dataset or model artifact was downloaded.

records.name: Auto-Research Arena
records.summary: Evaluates autonomous research harnesses across nine language-model efficiency objectives, separating quality and resource admissibility from target improvement. Records all launched experiments, including failures, and scores the best admissible candidate. Comparisons include six LLM-based harnesses and a restricted non-agentic baseline; simple sequential search remains competitive. Results concern compact pretraining programs, a fixed data pool and training seed, and specified hardware, rather than general scientific discovery.

records.name: EmbodiedLab
records.summary: Evaluates robot agents on 30 simulated experiments requiring manipulation, instrument readings, analysis, and evidence-linked answers. Success also requires restoring the bench. The best native-interface agent succeeds in 43.3% of tasks; interaction and restoration dominate attributed failures. Added skills reuse successful runs on the same experiments and serve a diagnostic comparison. Familiar simulator physics and coupled model–harness configurations limit generalization.

records.name: Labference
records.summary: A robotic-laboratory benchmark protocol connecting observed physical outcomes to subsequent operation choices, with separate selection, execution and completion measures. It defines controlled state pairs and matched support interventions across spatial, numerical and memory-dependent tasks. Current quantitative results concern initial simulated easy weighing; matched Oracle studies and wider task-family evaluation remain pending. Physical-robot recordings provide qualitative pilot examples.
records.status: The project page links a GitHub repository that returned 404 during review; public implementation availability is unverified. Collection demonstrations are not model-evaluation results.

records.name: SciValidityBench
records.summary: Generates experimental histories from 64 task specifications to test whether remembered evidence may validly guide a decision. Programmatic oracles and paired corruption, repair, and counterfactual controls distinguish retrieving a fact from using its governing context. Tests span five validity mechanisms and six domain settings. Results concern controlled decision tasks and explicit state compilation; transfer to real laboratory histories or end-to-end research remains open.
records.status: Official source includes task/state interfaces, scoring, and deterministic examples. Repository and paper were inspected without downloading datasets, installing dependencies, or executing the benchmark.

records.name: PersonaScienceBench
records.summary: Adapts 200 tasks from five benchmarks into interactions with simulated researchers while keeping each task’s objectives fixed across persona settings. Measures task performance, fact recovery and repetition. Actor and simulator share a model, so comparisons concern coupled systems. Most conditions have one rollout; incomplete outcomes and heterogeneous aggregation restrict scoreboard comparisons. The four profiles are contrasting configurations rather than representative human populations.
records.status: The evaluation uses simulated collaborators and bounded computational tasks, not human researcher trials. Public benchmark code and task-package availability were not established from the examined sources.

records.name: POSEIDON: Scaling Training Environments for Scientific Agents from Code Repositories
records.summary: Turns scientific repositories into reproduction, subflow, completion, and correction tasks using executable seed programs and iterative validation. The resulting Pearl collection supports supervised agent training, evaluated on six benchmark suites. A separate 600-environment human audit examines quality. Reported transfer depends on repository selection, generated evaluators, and benchmark exclusions; sample auditing does not certify every environment or establish autonomous scientific discovery.
records.status: The paper reports 97,659 training environments from 7,110 repositories, with intentional biological oversampling. An official implementation or Pearl download release was not established from the examined sources.

records.name: RIDAR
records.summary: Provides trajectory collectors, post-hoc integrity detection, runtime intervention, and a monitoring interface for research agents. Findings link to evidence in recorded runs, with public result files accompanying the implementation. It supports investigation of agent research behavior; detector output requires contextual review and does not certify scientific validity.
records.status: Official repository announces the code release on 23 October. No installation or runtime validation was performed here.

records.name: SCI-AGENT-EXAM
records.summary: A workflow-oriented benchmark of 120 expert-curated tasks across 11 fields and seven research activities. Agents must deliver executable outputs and scientific reports, evaluated through weighted deterministic checks and expert-authored rubrics applied by an LLM judge. Ten-model experiments show that report quality and executable correctness can diverge; trajectory snapshots further expose regressions. Scores describe the specified offline tasks and harness, with judge calibration bounded by the documented reference checks.
records.status: The paper claims code and data availability at SKYLENAGE-AI/Sci-Agent-Exam, but its public GitHub page and API both returned 404 on 27 October. Public artifact availability is unverified; no benchmark execution was performed.

records.name: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
records.summary: Combines retrieval of historical scientific designs, evolving start-selection strategies, and optimizer-program evolution under physical constraints. The authors evaluate gravitational-wave detector designs on eight held-out topologies using a differentiable simulator and matched scientific evaluation budgets. Results support optimization within this setting; transfer beyond simulation and dependence on historical-library coverage remain open.

records.name: GeoAgent: Contract-Constrained LLM Agents for Seismic Data Processing
records.summary: Connects seismic-processing tools through a fixed nine-stage graph, with explicit contracts for artifacts, input resolution, parameter ownership, and output validation. Deterministic geometry checks address failures that prompting alone did not prevent. Evidence comes from engineering measurements on one dataset and model family; adaptive planning, migration quality, and broader controlled comparisons remain unestablished.

records.name: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
records.summary: Trains text and vision models to predict acceptance from anonymized manuscripts, with stronger matched-source results from page images. ICLR inputs include rebuttal-era revisions, while arXiv rejection labels are inferred from missing proceedings matches. Accuracy concentrates at rating extremes and degrades across sources. The score estimates review outcomes; it does not establish correctness, novelty, or scientific impact.
records.status: The authors report NeurIPS 2026 acceptance. A proceedings record was not independently verified, so this entry retains the preprint source label. Results were inspected, not reproduced.

records.name: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
records.summary: Audits research trajectories with separate Analyzer and Verifier agents, then tests runtime feedback against matched unassisted runs. Its taxonomy covers 14 integrity violations. Reported findings depend on LLM judgments and mathematics/ML tasks; testing files and extra resources remain accessible deliberately, so detected violation rates should not be generalized to environments enforcing those boundaries.
records.status: Annotation follows the October arXiv preprint. An earlier ICLR 2027 submission was withdrawn; its title and reported results differ.

records.name: RIV-Gold
records.summary: Contains 60 research-agent trajectories annotated by 17 experts using the RIVT integrity taxonomy. Evaluation distinguishes finding-level matching from exact violation-type agreement, making it useful for testing trajectory auditors. The sampled mathematics and ML tasks constrain generalization; agreement with annotations is distinct from proving that a resulting scientific claim is correct.
records.status: Public auditor code and result files were verified; release of the full raw trajectories and annotation package was not established.

records.name: Astro2Method
records.summary: Tests ML-method selection on 500 expert-reviewed questions from 346 astronomy papers. Historical-paper retrieval and additional reasoning yield no consistent overall gain. Web-search improvements concentrate in cases retrieving the source paper, while method-masked pipeline context improves harder questions. Difficulty reflects completeness of source explanations; public-paper exposure and privileged pipeline information limit claims about prospective scientific reasoning.
records.status: The official dataset card exposes 500 test rows under CC BY 4.0. No dataset files were downloaded and no evaluation was run.

records.name: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
records.summary: Extracts interpretable idea factors from archived programs whose score differences remain unexplained, then uses bandit-selected edits and plateau-triggered exploration to guide program evolution. Evaluations cover eleven mathematical tasks and six machine-learning engineering tasks. Reported gains concern bounded executable objectives; the theoretical benefits require stated assumptions, and transfer to expensive scientific verification remains untested.
records.status: The paper identifies itself as an extended version of CausalEvolve (arXiv:2603.14575). An official implementation release was not established from the inspected sources.

records.name: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents
records.summary: Learns continuous reference solutions and constructs matching PDE problems through manufactured solutions, giving coding agents numerical feedback without solving every new reference problem. Evaluations cover Navier–Stokes and Vlasov–Poisson-type tasks and adaptations of existing PDE agents. Its reliability analysis assumes controlled distribution mismatch and independent evaluation data; success on generated problems does not establish accuracy across arbitrary physical regimes.

records.name: Recursive Flint
records.summary: An open-weight mixture-of-experts coding model built with Recursive’s Eureka Machine and a human team. The model card specifies 39.8B total parameters and approximately 2.5B active per token, including the output head. Included as a concrete automated-research output and reusable coding component; released weights and inference code do not independently validate the development process or reported performance.
records.status: Apache-2.0 weights and inference engine; no local execution or independent performance reproduction in this collection.

records.name: Agent4Sci
records.summary: Combines 25 tasks from 20 scientific ML benchmarks across 11 domains. Human-verified baselines and standardized environments support agent optimization, separate held-out evaluation, and trajectory auditing. It probes scientific hill-climbing under declared compute budgets; variable long-horizon runs and imperfect verification limit leaderboard interpretations and broader claims of autonomous discovery.
records.status: Public runner and author-linked data splits; underlying datasets retain their individual terms. No execution was performed here.

records.name: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
records.summary: Studies frontier coding agents improving scientific ML baselines in Agent4Sci, separating optimization, held-out evaluation, and trajectory auditing. Default gains are largely engineering-driven; targeted research skills produce more varied interventions. The study distinguishes metric improvement from scientific insight, with limitations from run variance, imperfect audits, task-specific skills, and the absence of a human-researcher baseline.
records.status: The arXiv comment names the NeurIPS 2026 E&D Track; a proceedings record was not verified, so the source label remains preprint.

records.name: Autonomous adaptive spectral analysis with an LLM agent for self-driving laboratories
records.summary: Uses an LLM to inspect spectra and diagnostics, adjust predefined fitting parameters within bounded retries, or abstain, while deterministic code calculates the physical quantity. On 203 archived film spectra, it retains 183 baseline values, recovers 16 failed analyses, and abstains on four. This retrospective, single-campaign study does not test live laboratory control or detection of physically incorrect results that pass numerical checks.
records.status: Linked code belongs to the earlier deterministic optical-analysis campaign. Agent instructions are in this paper’s supplementary information; a standalone release of the complete agent workflow was not established.

records.name: Bayesian Model Discovery with Language Models: Closing the Loop between Hypotheses and Experiments
records.summary: Combines LLM-proposed functional forms with numerical parameter fitting, evidence-weighted predictions, and experiment selection by joint information gain over models and parameters. Four benchmarks compare predictive error and structural recovery, with ablations of numerical feedback. Results depend on the candidate pool, priors, and observation model; containing the true law as a special case is explicitly distinguished from recovering its exact form.
records.status: Preprint v1 inspected. No official implementation release was established from the examined primary sources.

records.name: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
records.summary: Combines computational chemistry tools with session records, confirmed project knowledge, and human-reviewed rules reused across projects. Four case studies and controlled replays of four internal tasks examine the contribution of retained context. The authors explicitly position it as supervised research assistance; campaign-wide memory benefits remain unisolated, and complete docking records include unreleased collaborator results.

records.name: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Extracts atomic claims from published cancer-registry studies, executes reproduction analyses, and tests alternative analytical choices through agent-generated perturbations. SEER-Repro supplies the evaluation setting. The authors distinguish reproducing reported findings from assessing their sensitivity; flagged alternatives require expert review, and report-based grading does not independently verify the complete analysis code.

records.name: DFM-Bench
records.summary: Evaluates hypotheses, revisions, development paths, complete research runs, and contribution families, with computational delivery tracked separately. The public runner imports snapshots and prepares evidence packets for external judging. Proposal scores and contribution records do not confirm discoveries; the paper reports correlated AI review roles and pending independent calibration of the automated evaluator.

records.name: DiscoveryRSI
records.summary: Provides a public research harness with provider adapters, role prompts, a tool registry, replay storage, and domain adapters for hypothesis development. The accompanying DiscoveryRSI-27B checkpoint supports research planning and revision. Public components expose the workflow, but restricted datasets and private campaign traces are excluded; this collection has not executed the system.

records.name: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
records.summary: Develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent search, converts selected plans into Harbor tasks, and uses contribution-weighted offline model training and fixed-model workflow replay for later runs. DFM-Bench scores proposals and research histories. Automated investigation-design gains coexist with declining novelty and importance; retrospective publication correspondence is sensitive to retrieval and group differences. Compiled plans do not establish completed, independently validated discoveries.
records.status: Summary follows v2, revised 20 October 2026; date records the first submission on 16 October.

records.name: SEER-Repro
records.summary: Evaluates reproduction of 2,190 atomic claims from 20 published SEER-based studies using database documentation and executable analyses. Numerical tolerances and model-assisted evidence grading determine claim outcomes. Scores concern the selected papers and available registry release; matching reported claims does not establish robustness to alternative analyses or independent verification of all code.
records.status: Benchmark described in the preprint; a public code and benchmark-package release was not verified in the inspected sources.

records.name: PhysClosureBench
records.summary: Provides 50 physics research tasks with specified goals and constraints. A 20-criterion score measures local accomplishments, while a separate closure assessment tests whether essential evidence and applicability conditions resolve the research question. Model-based grading includes a selected human consistency check; high partial scores are not equivalent to complete scientific closure.
records.status: Execution framework and Case 30 example are public; the author-linked Hugging Face page provides the 50-case materials. Scientific grading is separate from the execution harness.

records.name: SciPIvot
records.summary: A scientific-judgment benchmark built from 248 human corrections across 26 research projects. Models choose between an original agent plan and a human-corrected alternative using the earlier project record. Five models often retain corrected mistakes, and added context or reconsideration does not consistently help. The challenge-set design evaluates recognition of selected corrections, rather than autonomous planning or the frequency of failures in research.

records.name: Agentic Scientist
records.summary: Orchestrates coding agents through investigation, ablations, sealed evaluation, analysis, and manuscript production. The public implementation includes task snapshots, resumable runs, and an inspection interface. It is useful for studying research orchestration and evidence collection; successful execution and scientific validity still depend on the task, evaluator, and underlying agent.

records.name: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
records.summary: Coordinates coding agents through typed hypothesis contracts, sandboxed experiments, shared memory, retrospective ablations, and evidence-linked manuscript audits. Evaluation includes 70 computational ML campaigns scored by an AI-reviewer proxy and separate held-out case studies. Its single accepted ALIFE paper involved substantial human specification, verification, statistical analysis, and editing; automated rubric gates also missed evaluation-protocol changes.

records.name: Brilliance for adaptive computational research in accelerator physics
records.summary: Combines reusable physics modules, agent-written programs, and JuTrack calculations to revise accelerator investigations. Cases include ideal storage-ring design and offline calibration against measured responses with a specialist reference. Detailed requests and further scientist guidance supply expertise. The sub-10-pm candidate retains momentum-acceptance limitations; finite tracking and single configuration comparisons do not establish operational readiness. Calibration agreement is not unique recovery of machine errors or residuals at measurement resolution.
records.status: Reviewed v3, revised 4 November 2026; the catalog date retains the original 11 October submission. Numerical research cases and offline calibration are distinct from commissioning or operating an accelerator.

records.name: AutoSciBench: Autonomous Benchmark Generation for Evaluating Scientific Agents
records.summary: Constructs scientific-agent tasks from high-level concepts and executable recipes, then revises them using solver trajectories and judge feedback. Experience from earlier refinements guides later generation across computational biology, materials science, and clinical imaging. The generator also serves as solver during refinement, and quality ratings come from LLM judges. Increased difficulty and favorable ratings do not independently establish scientific validity or broad evaluation coverage.
records.status: The paper describes generated tasks and evaluation procedures. A public implementation or downloadable task release was not established from the inspected primary sources.

records.name: Can AI Scientists Coordinate at Runtime?
records.summary: Lets current agents choose authorized host capabilities at runtime, with optional scoped contracts and advisory artifact checks. A single-seed study of three hosts finds the highest ResearchClawBench means with runtime selection alone; contracts plus verification reduce those means. Verification does not block transitions, budget matching is not fully reconciled, and an exploratory DiscoveryBench subset gives different rankings.

records.name: Denario Project: Deep Knowledge Artificial Intelligence Agents for Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Provides modular agents for ideation, literature checks, analysis, code execution, and paper drafting across supplied scientific datasets. Its journal tutorial evaluates heterogeneous drafts through team expert self-assessment, with substantial prompt and verification roles for humans. Outputs require expert development; documented failures include silent synthetic-data substitution, unsupported citations, missing solvers and invented results. The interdisciplinary demonstration is a single case.

records.name: Agentic AI–Physicist Collaboration in Experimental Particle Physics: A Proof-of-Concept Measurement with LEP Open Data
records.summary: Demonstrates an agent-assisted thrust analysis of archived ALEPH data, using supplied prior analyses, code execution, unfolding and manuscript drafting. Physicists define acceptance criteria, inspect outputs and approve scientific decisions. This is a supervised demonstration of a known observable, with no controlled productivity comparison; the paper’s descriptions of response-Monte-Carlo covariance and total uncertainty combination remain internally inconsistent.
records.status: Published in Highlights of High-Energy Physics, volume 2, issue 3, article 10, on 30 September 2026. The first preprint appeared on 5 March; v3 incorporates journal proofreading corrections.

records.name: ScientistTwo
records.summary: Coordinates limitation-driven hypotheses, experiments, ablations, and simulated review–rebuttal cycles. The study reports 86 successful improvements from 107 selected ML challenges, with most review comparisons conditioned on those successes. Human manuscript assessment adds evidence, while unmatched baseline pools and automated acceptance limit interpretation. Generated research artifacts are distinct from a released orchestration framework.

records.name: ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI
records.summary: Coordinates limitation-driven hypotheses, subset-to-full experiments, ablation-based refinement, and simulated review–rebuttal cycles that can trigger supplementary experiments. Across 107 selected ML-paper challenges, it reports 86 successful improvements; gains and most review scores condition on those successes. Acceptance figures come from automated reviewers, with a 33-paper human assessment; reported cost averages about $3,765 per completed NeurIPS-derived task.

records.name: ScienceBuddy
records.summary: Combines an interactive scientific workspace with research on alternating harness improvement and model reinforcement learning. The public repository distinguishes its hosted workspace demonstration from open experiments using frozen tasks and simulated feedback. It is especially relevant to human feedback and persistent research context; deployed continual improvement is not established by the released experiment alone.

records.name: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
records.summary: Provides a biomedical workspace that couples instruction/skill-harness revision with model reinforcement learning. Case studies report fixed-model adaptation, fixed-harness pass@4 gains, and three alternating update cycles on scientific QA tasks. Real researcher interactions illustrate task and rubric construction; the controlled adaptation experiment uses bounded simulated feedback, and individual feedback or skill contributions are not isolated.

records.name: IdeaForecastBench
records.summary: Evaluates whether ideas proposed from literature available before a cutoff correspond to later publications. It contains 624 rolling episodes across 52 topics, generates up to five ranked ideas, and reports separate judge results. This measures research forecasting under a retrospective protocol; broad or generic predictions and judge sensitivity complicate interpretation as precise scientific anticipation.
records.status: Published in the EMNLP 2026 proceedings. The final paper and appendices were appraised; retrospective idea correspondence depends on retrieval and model judgments, with current human calibration still limited.

records.name: ResearchStudio
records.summary: Microsoft’s ResearchStudio provides Idea for literature-grounded proposal development and Reel for editable posters, narrated videos, blogs, and an aligned viewer. Idea is assessed through automated proposal judgments; Reel’s quantitative study covers posters, while other outputs remain capability demonstrations. Their shared repository supports distinct research stages rather than establishing a fully autonomous experimental discovery pipeline.

records.name: Recursive Eureka Machine
records.summary: Recursive describes an automated research loop that proposes ideas, implements experiments, checks results, and carries useful context across parallel investigations. Public examples include training and GPU-kernel optimization; its later Flint model provides a released development outcome. Available research artifacts support inspection of selected outputs, but do not establish access to the complete research framework or independently verified autonomy.
records.status: Creator-reported system; public output artifacts are distinct from full framework source.

records.name: SoundnessBench
records.summary: Tests methodological judgments on 1,099 results-masked research proposals reconstructed from ICLR papers. Reviewer soundness scores provide proxy labels; 327 proposals also have proposal-only expert judgments. It separates false approvals from false rejections. Full-paper reviewers and proposal-only assessors see different evidence, and subjective labels limit interpretation as ground truth for scientific soundness.
records.status: Public proposal dataset and evaluation code verified. The v3 expert subset is described in the paper; its separate annotation release was not verified.

records.name: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
records.summary: Examines whether language models can assess methodological soundness before experiments are run. Results-masked proposals receive reviewer-derived proxy labels and separate expert judgments on a subset. Standard prompts favor approval, while aggressive prompts trade false approvals for false rejections. The study concerns proposal-stage judgment; its labels do not establish experimental truth or general research quality.
records.status: Reviewed v3, revised 23 October 2026; date retains the first arXiv submission on 28 May.

records.name: ScientistOne
records.summary: Links literature, code-search artifacts, and manuscript claims through evidence tags and integrity audits. Adapted ADRS evaluations include human correction of flagged audit results, while majority-vote checks miss a documented exploit. Transfer medal results use repeated test-grader feedback rather than the official single-submission protocol. Generated artifacts and complete framework availability remain separate questions.

records.name: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
records.summary: Links literature notes, code-search artifacts, and manuscript claims through a Chain-of-Evidence workflow and four-part integrity audit. In 75 adapted ADRS runs, it reports strong score reproduction and reference identity checks, with human correction of flagged audit results. Majority-vote checks still miss documented exploits; MLE-bench medal results use repeated test-grader feedback rather than the official single-submission protocol.

records.name: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
records.summary: Google’s Gemini-based Co-Scientist generates, critiques and evolves research hypotheses through literature search and Elo-ranked agent debates. Expert-guided evaluations include selected AML drug and combination assays, liver-organoid tests and rediscovery of unpublished antimicrobial-resistance findings. Human screening and laboratory work remain central; several candidates failed, biological effects were context dependent, and automated Elo scores do not establish general scientific correctness.

records.name: Computational Discovery (Google Labs)
records.summary: Hosted scientific-coding tool built with ERA and AlphaEvolve, announced through Google’s trusted-tester program. The November 2026 update documents MCP integration for approved users alongside browser access. It offers a route to delegate computational investigations from compatible agents; access is gated, and the collection did not use the service. Published ERA research and generated application artifacts should be distinguished from availability or independent validation of this hosted product.

records.name: Empirical Research Assistance: An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software
records.summary: Uses LLM code rewriting and tree search to improve supplied scientific evaluation metrics, incorporating expert guidance, paper summaries, and recombined ideas. Experiments report gains in single-cell integration, retrospective forecasting, and other computational tasks. Results depend on task-specific scoring and data splits; forecasting comparisons use dated retrospective data, and implementation audits disclose failures and departures from some proposed methods.

records.name: Robin: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
records.summary: Combines literature retrieval, LLM-ranked therapeutic hypotheses and notebook data-analysis agents in a human-run experimental loop. The Nature study reports phagocytosis-enhancing candidates in cultured retinal cells, including primary cells from one donor. Experts supply protocols, physical experiments, preprocessing and analysis prompts; these in-vitro findings do not establish clinical effectiveness, and broad productivity gains are estimated rather than measured against a human research team.

records.name: NORA: A Harness-Engineered Autonomous Research Agent for End-to-End Spatial Data Science
records.summary: Orchestrates spatial research through domain skills, persistent files, separate reviewers, and human checkpoints. Three case studies demonstrate useful workflow assistance while recording substantial expert intervention and lower human ratings of rigor than LLM ratings. Ablations are qualitative. Generated reports retain unresolved validation issues, including an invalid fairness-bound argument and uncalibrated elevation uncertainty, so workflow completion should not be treated as verified scientific discovery.

records.name: PaperOrchestra
records.summary: Turns supplied ideas and experimental records into LaTeX manuscripts using planning, literature, plotting, writing, and refinement agents. On a benchmark reconstructed from 200 accepted papers, human reviewers prefer its drafts to two writing baselines. These comparisons assess manuscript quality; citation-identity checks and simulated acceptance do not validate underlying science, and generated figures and model-driven refinement require independent review.

records.name: LitPivot: Developing Well-Situated Research Ideas Through Dynamic Contextualization and Critique within the Literature Landscape
records.summary: Links proposal editing to changing literature: researchers select problem, contribution, or evaluation facets, inspect relevant paper clusters, and consider excerpt-backed critiques and revisions. A 17-participant study reports stronger expert-rated literature grounding, with a five-participant qualitative follow-up. Novelty benefits are self-reported; short HCI/NLP ideation tasks do not establish feasibility, successful experiments, or long-term research impact.
records.status: UIST 2026 proceedings identity verified from ACM-deposited DOI metadata, matching the author manuscript. The current author version was read, but the publisher PDF and separately promised study-protocol supplement remain unavailable. Prototype source or access was not established.

records.name: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
records.summary: Combines template-based and template-free agents for research ideas, experiments, manuscripts, and automated review. The Nature paper consolidates earlier AI Scientist reports and adds analyses; its workshop campaign overlaps v2. One selected manuscript received acceptance-level reviews before withdrawal. Human selection, code and data errors, and model-based evaluation constrain claims of independent scientific validation.

records.name: OpenScientist: evaluating an open agentic AI co-scientist to accelerate biomedical discovery
records.summary: Evaluates an open hypothesis-testing agent on four featured biomedical case studies and three supplementary cases, combining data analysis, literature retrieval, and reports. Expert review identifies useful results alongside preprocessing mistakes, statistical weaknesses, and incomplete rejection on randomized controls. Selected cases and human prompt/data refinement limit generalization; estimated time savings are not a controlled productivity comparison.
records.status: medRxiv v1 was posted on 18 March 2026, as confirmed by the publisher metadata API; the DOI date fragment is not the posting date. Full text was read through Europe PMC. No independent reproduction was performed.

records.name: RINoBench
records.summary: Tests novelty judgments on 1,381 ideas extracted by an LLM from ICLR submissions, paired with binned reviewer scores and model-synthesized explanations. Nine metrics assess score agreement and justifications against supplied related-work abstracts. Models produce plausible explanations while poorly matching novelty ratings. These are subjective, filtered machine-learning review labels, with further LLM processing and grading; they do not measure universal novelty or scientific validity.

records.name: EvoScientist: Towards Multi-Agent Evolving AI Scientists for End-to-End Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Coordinates a researcher, engineer and evolution manager that turn prior idea reviews and execution trajectories into retrievable ideation and experimentation memories. On 30 curated AI queries, it reports stronger judged ideas and higher mean code-execution success after memory updates. Human comparisons cover four baselines; selected conference-track acceptances are case evidence, and execution success does not establish scientific correctness or cross-domain autonomous discovery.

records.name: MOOSE-Star: Unlocking Tractable Training for Scientific Discovery by Breaking the Complexity Barrier
records.summary: Trains hypothesis generation through decomposed discovery subtasks, motivation-guided hierarchical retrieval, and bounded composition. TOMATO-Star supplies paper-derived supervision; evaluations measure retrieval and LLM-scored reconstruction of held-out hypotheses. The best-case complexity reduction relies on compositional and routing assumptions, and the study does not prospectively validate new discoveries.

records.name: FIRE-Bench
records.summary: Asks research agents to rediscover published empirical findings from high-level questions while withholding original procedures and conclusions. Research-problem trees define tasks; LLM claim extraction and entailment generate reference-aligned precision, recall and F1. Human checks cover extraction on a subset, rather than end-to-end scientific validity. Valid alternative findings can be penalized, and inspected software inventories differ from the paper’s evaluated tasks.
records.status: The date records the first preprint; the ICML 2026 proceedings record establishes peer review. The paper reports 40 executed tasks and 60 additional parsed papers. README snapshot a7017c95f680 instead lists 35 hand-curated tasks and 153 unverified generated tasks; these inventories are not assumed equivalent. No benchmark or dataset was executed or downloaded.

records.name: AIDE (scientific data curation)
records.summary: Public data-curation pipeline searches Hugging Face datasets, applies a model-based quality gate, and generates processing code for retrieval or instruction formats. The documented outputs retain selected sources, processors, organized data, and logs; paper evaluations use separate downstream tools. This is the Agentic Intelligent Data Engine, distinct from WecoAI’s AIDE search agent. Model services and data access are required for full curation; no runtime was executed here.

records.name: auto_research (high-energy astrophysics)
records.summary: Public orchestration code connects research agents to a separate analysis toolkit, checks generated tools, and validates report provenance. Tool changes enter a working branch; trusted promotion remains a human decision. The documented deployment needs configured model services and astronomy software. Source availability supports inspection, while the paper’s event logs and planted-defect review records are request-only and no execution was performed for this collection.

records.name: AutoIllustrate
records.summary: Converts a method description into an editable draw.io diagram, then optionally applies an image-generation restyling pass. The public command-line workflow includes figure generation and visual auditing and was used with Agentic Scientist. Retaining the vector source supports manual correction, but generated visual polish should not be taken as evidence of methodological fidelity.

records.name: Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap
records.summary: Examines computational research agents through autonomy, evaluation, released artifacts, human intervention, novelty checks, and result-selection disclosure. Its coded corpus distinguishes runnable code from evidence that supports scientific claims. The conclusions are bounded by the screened AI/ML systems and coding rules, rather than a census of all scientific domains.

records.name: Brilliance
records.summary: Public conversational accelerator-research framework connects agent-written Python programs to JuTrack numerical services, reusable expert modules, and persistent project evidence. The documented installation requires Julia, scientific dependencies, and a configured model backend. Scientists can inspect calculations and redirect investigations. The paper evaluates simulation and offline measured-response calibration; neither source availability nor the example gallery demonstrates independent reproduction or live accelerator operation.

records.name: Claim-to-evidence checker
records.summary: Extracts numerical result claims, indexes recorded result files, and compares value matches with contextual provenance scores and per-claim decoys. Frozen operating points support certification and audit outputs. It is useful for reviewing research reports against their saved artifacts; unsupported matches need contextual review, and incomplete logs or extraction failures can leave correct claims uncertified.
records.status: Public checker tree and README inspected at e6253daa687e without execution. The repository releases derived data and labels rather than redistributing the benchmark’s raw submissions. Precise initial software-release date was not established.

records.name: ClaimNov
records.summary: Provides reusable claim extraction, reference-pool retrieval, entailment scoring, and proposal verdict functions. Reports retain matched papers and claim-level evidence, while evaluation scripts support comparison with existing novelty checks. Researchers supply the prior-work pool and model services. Scores describe coverage by that pool; they neither certify universal novelty nor validate scientific correctness.
records.status: README and pipeline inspected at 413f16c7f94b without installation or model calls. Precise initial software-release date was not established.

records.name: DefectSkills
records.summary: Provides reusable prompts, human decision points, and optional reference scripts for VASP-based point-defect calculations. The public release contains the workflow manuscript and supporting analysis files; running it requires a configured scientific-computing environment and appropriate VASP access. It is guidance for an agent, rather than a standalone autonomous engine, and the reported demonstration still required scientific and execution corrections.

records.name: Magnolia
records.summary: Adds readable project notebooks, reviewed memory promotion, scientific-tool wrappers, and local or Slurm job tracking to an OpenCode-based workflow. Two MCP services expose memory and computational operations while preserving run provenance. Researchers direct the work and approve standing rules; the claim critic and promotion panel do not establish scientific correctness, and adaptation to another harness requires additional integration.
records.status: Public research software; no installation or execution was performed. The paper explicitly disclaims autonomy, so the catalog treats this as supporting research infrastructure. Precise initial release date not established.

records.name: MUSE
records.summary: Provides memory construction, consolidation, retrieval, and gate components with prompts and structured schemas. A scientific coding agent supplies the task and tool interactions; the gate can return focused review advice or skip injection. The release supports integration and inspection, while benchmark environments and verifiers are separate dependencies. Component availability does not by itself reproduce the paper’s full evaluation.
records.status: Public README and component tree inspected at 524ddcd70fa5 without installation, model calls, or benchmark execution. Precise initial software-release date was not established.

records.name: NORA (spatial data science)
records.summary: Coordinates spatial research through domain skills, persistent project files, separate reviewers, and nine human checkpoints. Three cases demonstrate workflow assistance with substantive expert intervention; human rigor ratings are lower than model ratings, and ablations are qualitative. Generated reports retain validation problems, including an invalid fairness-bound argument, so completed workflows require independent scientific checking.

records.name: OpenResearch
records.summary: A local research workspace and harness from alphaXiv that connects coding agents to literature discovery, experiment execution, and artifact inspection. It records experiments in a local database and supports multiple compute backends. The repository documents a usable product; these capabilities are project claims rather than an independently established discovery benchmark.

records.name: OpenScientist
records.summary: Runs iterative investigations from researcher questions and optional datasets, combining executable analysis, PubMed retrieval, hypothesis tracking, persistent research state, and final reports. The inspected code supports feedback between iterations and database-backed knowledge records. Public source supports inspection and self-hosting; the biomedical preprint evaluates an earlier configuration, and recorded findings or matched citations do not independently establish scientific validity.
records.status: Implementation inspected at commit 9513b998cea5 without execution. The year identifies the documented 2026 implementation, not an established first public release date. The hosted service was not tested.

records.name: PaperBanana
records.summary: Uses retrieval, planning, styling, visualization, and critique agents to generate academic diagrams and plots from scientific content. Its repository includes execution interfaces and a benchmark of reference illustrations. It is a useful study of iterative visual communication, with semantic accuracy and faithful representation of experimental data still requiring inspection beyond aesthetic judgments.
records.status: Published at ICML 2026 (PMLR 306). The final paper and substantive appendices were appraised; illustration and plot evaluations do not certify every generated technical detail.

records.name: PaperScorer
records.summary: Packages manuscript preparation, acceptance scoring, an agent-assisted review interface, and optional literature reranking behind a command-line orchestrator. It accepts PDFs, LaTeX projects, or arXiv identifiers and supports comparison across manuscript commits. Released source enables inspection; score changes describe predicted review outcomes, and generated critiques still require evidence checking rather than being treated as validated scientific judgments.
records.status: MIT-licensed implementation and documentation inspected at f76d60e4e051 without installation or model execution. The repository links model and dataset releases; those artifacts were not downloaded. Precise initial software-release date was not established.

records.name: PDE-GAV
records.summary: Provides a configurable PDE experimentation environment with public-input queries, private reference evaluation, candidate selection, run logs, and interfaces for new equations and tasks. The repository documents a deterministic CPU demonstration and scientific campaign configurations. Large datasets, weights, and complete historical execution archives are external; public code availability alone does not reproduce the paper’s experiments.
records.status: Official repository and documentation inspected without installation or execution. Only the release year is recorded; a precise initial software-release date was not established.

records.name: SpectralColorLab
records.summary: Supplies Windows acquisition software, Android AR stimulus control, and iPad USB/SSH helpers for acknowledged color holds and spectrometer sampling. Synthetic RGB definitions support reconstructing stimulus protocols; calibrated hardware and vendor SDKs must be provided separately. Useful for building inspectable measurement interfaces. Released source excludes observed measurements, fitted models, and calibration, so software availability does not reproduce the optical results or establish a complete recursive research-agent framework.
records.status: Source and README inspected at 255a2f896040 without installation or execution. The represented software is from 2026; a precise first-public-release date was not established. Device acknowledgements verify rendering state, not calibrated optical emission or physical settling.

records.name: AInsteinBench
records.summary: Evaluates scientific software development with 244 tasks from maintainer pull requests and synthesized feature-completion exercises across six research codebases. Containerized tests assess patches, while expert review and case studies examine scientific invariants and test defects. This measures repository implementation under specified tests; passing does not establish correctness beyond their coverage or autonomous hypothesis selection.
records.status: Public evaluation code and question files; the README states that Docker images for Multi-SWE-bench-format questions are available upon request.

records.name: FrontierScience
records.summary: Assesses expert-level physics, chemistry, and biology reasoning using Olympiad and Research splits. The released gold sets contain 100 short-answer questions and 60 research subtasks, with model grading against answers or rubrics. These constrained, expert-authored tasks probe scientific reasoning; the creators explicitly distinguish them from the broader work of producing new discoveries.

records.name: Kosmos
records.summary: Coordinates parallel literature and data-analysis agents through a persistent world model. Seven selected studies include reproduced findings and new hypotheses, assessed through sampled human reanalysis and external validation. Researchers curate inputs, one final report is manually assembled, and productivity equivalents are collaborator estimates. Traceable artifacts support scrutiny without guaranteeing every interpretation or a general discovery yield.

records.name: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
records.summary: Coordinates parallel literature and data-analysis agents through a structured world model to produce source-linked discovery reports from human-curated datasets. Seven case studies include reproduced findings and new hypotheses, with human reanalysis and external validation. Experts supported79.4% of102 sampled statements, with lower interpretation accuracy; reported months of saved work are collaborator estimates, and one final discovery report involved manual curation.

records.name: A Survey of AI Scientists
records.summary: Synthesizes AI-scientist systems through six stages covering literature, ideas, preparation, execution, writing, and paper generation. The revised survey traces the shift from individual components to integrated workflows and discusses robustness and governance. Its stage-based organization is useful for comparing coverage, but does not make unlike evaluation settings directly comparable.

records.name: From AI for Science to Agentic Science: A Survey on Autonomous Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Organizes agentic science across life sciences, chemistry, materials, and physics, connecting capability, workflow, and domain perspectives. It provides a useful map of hypothesis generation, experimentation, analysis, and refinement. As a survey, its taxonomy helps navigate reported systems rather than independently reproducing their discovery or autonomy claims.

records.name: The Virtual Lab of AI agents designs new SARS-CoV-2 nanobodies
records.summary: Organizes a principal-investigator agent and scientific specialists into meetings with high-level human guidance. The agents develop a computational nanobody-design workflow, with selected designs tested experimentally. This demonstrates a specific human-AI research collaboration; human laboratory work and biological validation are central parts of the evidence.

records.name: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
records.summary: Recruits researchers to execute randomly assigned human- or model-generated NLP ideas, then obtains blinded reviews of the resulting projects. AI proposals show larger declines from ideation ratings, but final project-level differences are not statistically conclusive. Attrition, implementation changes, and differences between review stages qualify interpretation; the study demonstrates why proposal ratings alone are weak proxies for completed research quality.
records.status: ICLR 2026 publication identity verified. The displayed date remains the first preprint; version-comparison limits are recorded in the full-text notes.

records.name: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
records.summary: Evolves candidate programs using language-model edits and feedback from executable evaluators. Applications include mathematical constructions, algorithm discovery, and infrastructure optimization. The white paper illustrates breadth when a reliable scoring procedure exists; reported improvements are tied to those tasks and do not imply autonomous formulation of every scientific objective.

records.name: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
records.summary: Combines retrieval-guided planning and executable code with an environment of biomedical tools, software, and databases. Evaluations span heterogeneous tasks, multimodal data analysis, and experimental protocol design. The reported breadth supports biomedical research assistance; benchmark performance and protocol case studies should not be treated as general clinical validation.

records.name: ScienceBoard
records.summary: A desktop environment and 169-task benchmark for scientific software use across six domains. Agents act through GUI or command-line interfaces using screenshots, accessibility trees or marked images; application-state and output checks determine completion. Experiments expose grounding, software-knowledge and interface-selection difficulties, with improvements from hybrid interfaces and separated planning/grounding. These results concern bounded digital workflows; revised tables and older headline prose report different aggregate rates.
records.status: The later ScienceCUA preprint reports an audit and repairs, introducing ScienceBoard-Verified and ScienceBoard-VE. This record retains the original benchmark and task count; comparisons should identify the benchmark version.

records.name: MOOSE-Chem2: Exploring LLM Limits in Fine-Grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery via Hierarchical Search
records.summary: Expands coarse research directions into increasingly detailed hypotheses through hierarchical search, comparing different language-model scoring ensembles. Evaluation uses expert-annotated fine-grained hypotheses from recent literature. The study tests alignment with known hypotheses and model-defined rewards; a detailed, high-scoring proposal still needs independent checks and experimental testing.

records.name: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation
records.summary: Combines literature/code analysis, concept-to-implementation mapping, iterative advisor-guided experiments, and hierarchical manuscript drafting. Scientist-Bench evaluates guided and reference-only ML research tasks using execution checks and LLM rubric/pairwise judgments. Reported completion differs from correctness, reviewer preferences vary substantially, and benchmark prompts can expose target-method details; the study does not independently establish human-level scientific quality.

records.name: Scientist-Bench
records.summary: Introduced with AI-Researcher, this benchmark derives guided innovation and open-ended exploration tasks from AI research papers, supplying references, instructions, and datasets. The initial paper evaluates 22 reference papers and six open-ended tasks. Implementation assessments and comparative manuscript judgments cover several workflow stages, but judge-rated similarity to human research is not independent confirmation of novel scientific findings.

records.name: AI Idea Bench 2025
records.summary: Evaluates AI research idea generation using 3,495 target papers and their motivating references. Its protocol compares generated ideas with paper content and reference-based judgments, including novelty and feasibility assessments. Historical alignment provides a repeatable proxy for ideation quality, but resemblance to published work cannot establish prospective novelty, successful execution, or future scientific impact.

records.name: MLRC-Bench
records.summary: Adapts seven ML competitions into repository-level research tasks with protected evaluators and held-out testing. It measures improvement relative to baseline and top human solutions, and contrasts executed performance with LLM assessments of idea quality. Results are best-of-eight attempts; pass@k counts a 5% closure of the human-performance gap. Competition gains provide objective task evidence, while research novelty and transfer beyond these seven tasks require separate evaluation.

records.name: The AI Scientist-v2
records.summary: Uses staged tree search, debugging, replication, and visual feedback to develop experiments and manuscripts from supplied research topics. Humans selected three ideas and the best completed outputs for workshop review; one passed, and all were withdrawn under the agreed protocol. Internal audits expose leakage and claim–code mismatches, qualifying the evidence from selected manuscript acceptance.

records.name: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
records.summary: Replaces code templates with staged agentic tree search, replication nodes, and visual feedback for experiments and manuscripts. Humans selected three ideas and the best outputs from multiple autonomous runs for workshop review; one passed and was withdrawn as agreed. Internal audits document train/test overlap, misdescribed methods, and claimed experiments absent from successful code, so acceptance is bounded evidence of workshop-level manuscript quality.

records.name: PaperBench
records.summary: Measures reconstruction of 20 ML papers from scratch using author-approved rubrics, clean-environment execution, and an LLM grader. Scores combine partial credit for code, execution, and result matching; they are not the fraction of papers fully reproduced. Human comparisons cover a small selected subset with different selection and time budgets. The cheaper Code-Dev variant omits execution and result verification.

records.name: SciReplicate-Bench
records.summary: Assesses algorithm comprehension and implementation through 100 tasks extracted from 36 NLP papers published in 2024. Evaluation combines executable tests, reasoning-graph comparison, and repository dependency or API measures. Its scope is reproducing selected algorithmic components from papers; passing those tasks does not imply that every experiment or headline paper result was replicated.

records.name: AgentRxiv: Towards Collaborative Autonomous Research
records.summary: Adds a searchable shared report archive to Agent Laboratory so sequential or parallel research agents can reuse earlier findings. Prompting-search experiments improve best-so-far MATH-500 accuracy and show mixed transfer to other QA benchmarks. The target test set guides repeated search, parallel runs use more resources, and humans manually verify code and outputs because agents can fabricate results or remove essential method logic.

records.name: BixBench
records.summary: Evaluates bioinformatics agents on 61 expert-curated analysis scenarios with 205 associated questions. Agents explore supplied data and run notebook analyses; open responses are graded against reference answers, with separate multiple-choice experiments. The tested models reach about 21% open-answer accuracy. Shared-scenario questions and model-based judging limit interpretation, and prepared analysis success does not validate new biological mechanisms or experimental discoveries.

records.name: Google Co-Scientist
records.summary: A Gemini-based system in which agents generate, critique, rank, and refine scientific hypotheses in collaboration with researchers. Google describes biological case studies and an experimental Hypothesis Generation access route. This is a hosted research partner focused on hypothesis development; a general open-source implementation of Google's system was not confirmed.

records.name: Agent Laboratory
records.summary: Organizes specialist agents around literature review, planning, experimentation, and reporting for a researcher-supplied idea. The open implementation supports human feedback during the workflow and machine-learning experimentation. It provides a concrete research-assistant baseline; the quality and efficiency claims in its paper should be interpreted within the evaluated tasks and model configurations.

records.name: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
records.summary: Assists a human-supplied research idea through literature review, iterative ML coding, and report drafting, with optional feedback checkpoints. Small human studies find useful outputs but substantially lower paper-quality scores than automated reviewers; co-pilot gains concentrate in quality and presentation. Separate MLE-bench tests evaluate the solver component, while reported cost savings compare different workflow settings rather than matched scientific outcomes.

records.name: AIDE
records.summary: Searches executable ML solutions through draft, debug, and improvement branches scored by a supplied metric. Author Kaggle experiments and separately reported MLE-Bench/RE-Bench evaluations support bounded engineering utility. Historical leaderboard comparisons use differing holdouts and retain contamination risks; task-level labels in one table conflict with its definition. Results depend on model, budget, evaluator, and search space, and do not establish autonomous selection of scientific questions.

records.name: Biomni
records.summary: A biomedical research agent that combines retrieval-guided planning with executable code and a broad scientific software environment. Its repository exposes the agent, environment setup, tutorials, and supported research workflows. It is useful for investigating tool-rich biological analysis; biomedical task demonstrations do not establish clinical safety or reliability across all research domains.

records.name: OpenEvolve
records.summary: An open community implementation inspired by AlphaEvolve that evolves programs using language models, evaluator feedback, and population-based search. It includes examples for mathematical optimization, scientific computing, and kernel improvement. The repository is independently maintained rather than Google's original system, and its reported improvements should be checked against the corresponding evaluator and hardware conditions.

records.name: R&D-Agent
records.summary: A modular framework for autonomous machine-learning engineering that separates idea search from implementation and feedback. Its tested agent combines adaptive parallel exploration, structured hypothesis generation, collaborative memory, sampled-data debugging and standardized solution selection. MLE-Bench experiments report competition-medal gains with matched ML-Master reruns and selected-subset ablations. The evidence concerns bounded data-science optimization, with historical comparisons subject to differing models, hardware and budgets.

records.name: ShinkaEvolve
records.summary: Evolves programs against human-defined executable objectives using island archives, language-model mutations, novelty rejection, and adaptive model selection. Experiments cover circle packing, AIME scaffolds, ALE-Bench solutions, and MoE load balancing. Reported gains are task-dependent: exact circle-packing validation requires postprocessing, and the AIME 2025 scaffold trails majority voting. Open code supports local or cluster evaluation.
records.status: ICLR 2026 publication identity verified. The complete original preprint was appraised; changes in the inaccessible final paper and supplement remain unverified.

records.name: ToolUniverse
records.summary: Provides a common interface for scientific tools, datasets, models, and APIs so language-model agents can discover and invoke external capabilities. The public project offers a Python SDK and agent integrations. It supplies infrastructure for building scientific assistants; available tool connectors do not by themselves establish reliable tool selection, valid analyses, or experimental reproducibility.

records.name: Virtual Lab
records.summary: Structures collaboration between a human researcher and specialist language-model agents through team and individual meetings. The public code includes the nanobody-design application accompanying a Nature study with experimental validation. This supplies a grounded example of collaborative scientific discovery, while the biological evidence applies to that specific campaign rather than unrestricted autonomous laboratory work.

records.name: Autonomous LLM-driven research from data to human-verifiable research papers
records.summary: Guides agents from annotated data through hypotheses, analysis code, and manuscripts while linking numeric results back to producing code. Repeated case studies show fewer major errors for simple tasks, limited novelty, and failures on complex data or goals that require human review. The evaluated workflow includes prepared metadata and step approvals; traceability supports verification without establishing scientific correctness.

records.name: RE-Bench
records.summary: Compares agents with human experts on seven open-ended machine-learning research engineering environments, including optimization tasks with executable scoring functions. Its human-attempt data and multiple time budgets make resource assumptions visible. Results concern bounded AI research engineering, and rankings can change with time allowance; they do not establish general scientific autonomy.

records.name: CycleResearcher: Improving Automated Research via Automated Review
records.summary: Trains research-writing and reviewing models through supervised learning and iterative preference optimization. Main evaluations score manuscripts whose experimental results are deliberately fabricated, so simulated acceptance measures writing and reviewer alignment. Human reviewers rate selected outputs below typical submissions. A separate executed appendix example uses an external coding agent, but contains numerical and interpretation errors that limit claims of validated discovery.

records.name: MLE-bench
records.summary: Packages 75 Kaggle competitions to assess dataset preparation, model training, and iterative experimentation, with historical leaderboard thresholds as reference points. Useful for engineering-focused research agents and resource-scaling studies. A competition medal measures predictive performance under a particular setup; it is not evidence of novel hypotheses or scientific validity beyond that task.

records.name: MOOSE-Chem: Large Language Models for Rediscovering Unseen Chemistry Scientific Hypotheses
records.summary: MOOSE-Chem retrieves paper inspirations and evolves chemistry hypotheses through LLM mutation, critique and recombination. On 51 retrospectively decomposed papers it recovers parts of known innovations, but evaluation seeds the literature corpus with the true inspirations and selects candidates using answer-aware similarity scores. Expert ratings are lower than automatic scores, ranking remains weak, and proposed chemistry is not experimentally validated.

records.name: ScienceAgentBench
records.summary: A 102-task benchmark for generating executable Python programs that process, analyze and visualize scientific data across four disciplines. Expert validation, dataset modifications, task-specific outcome checks and human process rubrics support evaluation. Comparisons of prompting, self-debug and OpenHands show that successful execution can still produce scientifically incorrect results.
