Reported headline success uses the best of three attempts; tasks and source materials cover a bounded portion of scientific workflows.

records.name: Scideator: Human-LLM Compound System for Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation
records.summary: Extracts purpose, mechanism, and evaluation facets from papers so researchers can recombine ideas and inspect related work for novelty. A 22-person CS study reports greater perceived creativity support than a bundled baseline; separate ablations test retrieval and classification. Novelty confidence and several idea-quality ratings do not improve, and neither the study nor its retrieval-based labels validate completed scientific results.

records.name: CORE-Bench
records.summary: A computational-reproducibility benchmark with 270 tasks formed by three assistance levels over 90 scientific code packages. Agents recover selected outputs from known reproducible CodeOcean capsules, ranging from reading supplied results to installing dependencies and executing code. Original AutoGPT and CORE-Agent experiments expose environment and result-retrieval failures. The task construction tests selected output recovery, and a distinct 2026 companion revises shortcut-prone or incorrectly graded tasks.

records.name: PaperQA2
records.summary: Searches papers iteratively, summarizes and reranks evidence, traverses citations, and produces cited answers. LitQA2 evaluation finds higher answer precision than human annotators, with comparable overall accuracy. WikiCrow and ContraCrow extend the approach to summaries and contradiction screening; human agreement depends on the evidence and reasoning shown. The evaluated configuration and accessible full-text corpus differ from a default open-package installation.

records.name: SciAgents: Automating Scientific Discovery Through Bioinspired Multi-Agent Intelligent Graph Reasoning
records.summary: SciAgents uses knowledge-graph paths and specialized LLM agents to generate, expand and critique biologically inspired materials proposals. A literature-search assistant assigns novelty and feasibility scores to illustrative examples. Reported mechanical, optical and energy improvements are predictions; the study does not synthesize materials, execute the proposed simulations or independently establish superiority over human research.
records.status: Journal publication verified in Advanced Materials 37, article 2413523 (2025), first published online on 18 December 2024. The displayed date remains the 9 September 2024 first preprint. Publication status does not establish experimental realization of the proposed materials.

records.name: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
records.summary: Compares expert-written NLP prompting proposals with selected agent-generated proposals in blinded reviews involving 104 researchers. AI proposals receive higher novelty ratings across several analyses; lower feasibility estimates are not statistically conclusive. Limited idea diversity, unreliable automatic ranking, and unfaithful execution-agent implementations constrain interpretation. The study measures perceived proposal quality rather than demonstrated scientific outcomes.

records.name: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Uses human-prepared ML experiment templates, literature-assisted ideation, Aider code edits, experiment logs, and LaTeX generation to produce papers and automated reviews. Three small computational task families show substantial execution and writing attrition; reported acceptance thresholds come from its own reviewer. The paper documents metric errors, implementation mistakes, data leakage, hallucinated details, and unsafe execution behavior requiring human checks.

records.name: SciCode
records.summary: Uses 80 scientist-authored research coding problems, decomposed into 338 subproblems across 16 subfields, to test scientific knowledge and executable implementation. Report main-problem and subproblem accuracy separately, including whether background information was supplied. This assesses specified computational tasks; the later SciCode-Verified audit also makes benchmark version and test defects relevant to comparisons.

records.name: LAB-Bench
records.summary: Collects 2,457 multiple-choice tasks spanning literature, figures, tables, databases, protocols and biological sequences. Original baselines compare tool-free language models with experts allowed web and research tools, so the human gap is not a matched agent comparison. Small free-response checks expose distractor-based guessing. These bounded questions do not establish laboratory execution, complete biological research, or novel experimental validation.

records.name: DiscoveryBench
records.summary: Tests hypothesis discovery from supplied datasets, metadata, and natural-language goals using 264 literature-derived tasks across six domains, plus 903 synthetic tasks. Facet-based evaluation separates aspects of a proposed finding. The target is recovering supported relationships within provided data, with synthetic and real tasks reported separately, rather than discovering unrestricted new scientific knowledge.

records.name: BioDiscoveryAgent: An AI Agent for Designing Genetic Perturbation Experiments
records.summary: Uses an LLM to select genetic perturbation batches, incorporate observed phenotypes, and optionally retrieve literature, search gene databases, or critique selections. Retrospective replay across six single-gene screens and one paired-gene screen measures hit discovery against optimization and random baselines. Gains depend on dataset, model, and budget; added tools can hurt stronger models, and the study does not establish prospective autonomous biological discovery.

records.name: ChemCrow: Augmenting large language models with chemistry tools
records.summary: ChemCrow equips GPT-4 with chemistry tools for retrieval, molecular analysis, synthesis planning and robotic execution. It synthesized four known compounds and helped a human-guided workflow identify a new chromophore, whose absorption differed by 33 nm from the target. Expert evaluations favour factuality over tool-free GPT-4, but reasoning failures persist; laboratory oversight and proprietary services remain necessary, and the public release includes only 12 of 18 tools.

records.name: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
records.summary: ResearchAgent combines citation-linked paper abstracts, retrieved entities and LLM reviewers to draft and iteratively refine research problems, methods and experiment plans. Human and model evaluations favour the full GPT-4 system over simpler variants, while weaker backbones benefit inconsistently. Evidence concerns proposal ratings; the system does not execute experiments, and entity-linking noise and reviewer agreement limit claims of scientific validity.

records.name: Docling
records.summary: Converts documents into structured representations using page-layout analysis, table reconstruction, optional OCR, and typed assembly. Its technical report benchmarks runtime on five documents totaling 225 pages with OCR disabled, rather than establishing general extraction accuracy. Published examples omit figure text and break a cross-column paragraph; Markdown repeats spanning headers while JSON retains spans. Current software capabilities should be checked separately from this historical report.

records.name: MLAgentBench
records.summary: An executable benchmark of 13 machine-learning experimentation tasks with starter code, data and automatic evaluators. A ReAct-derived agent reads, edits and runs experiments while maintaining plans and fact-check statements. Eight-trial experiments across seven backbones show strong task dependence, with better results on established datasets than several newer challenges. The benchmark measures bounded optimization tasks; qualitative traces expose persistent planning, interpretation and submission errors despite explicit checking prompts.

records.name: OpenScholar
records.summary: A scientific-literature synthesis system combining specialized retrieval, reranking, citation-linked generation and iterative feedback. The author-linked preprint evaluates answer quality, attribution and expert preference across several disciplines, while documenting persistent factuality and retrieval limitations. Human preference chiefly reflects coverage and presentation, rather than independently verified correctness. The later Nature publication is linked by the authors, but its main text and supplements remain unread in this audit.

records.name: STORM / Co-STORM
records.summary: STORM develops cited articles through perspective-guided questions, web-grounded conversations, and outline refinement. Its Co-STORM companion lets users steer simulated-expert discussions and organizes findings in a shared mind map. Evaluations support aspects of organization and user preference; small human studies and model-based grading do not establish objective learning gains, complete factual accuracy, or publication-ready scientific reporting.

records.name: The AI Scientist
records.summary: Implements a template-based loop for proposing ideas, changing experimental code, running machine-learning experiments, and drafting papers with an automated reviewer. The repository provides executable workflows and example outputs. Its structured starting templates make it a useful baseline for research automation, while generated manuscripts still require inspection of results, citations, and methodological claims.

records.name: Coscientist: Autonomous chemical research with large language models
records.summary: Coscientist connects GPT-4 planning, web and documentation search, code execution and laboratory APIs. It executes known coupling reactions and bounded instrument tasks, with researcher-prepared resources, manual plate movement and occasional guidance. Reaction-optimization results use previously collected datasets rather than a live laboratory loop. Only a simplified implementation is released, and the demonstrations do not establish autonomous novel chemical discovery.

records.name: FunSearch: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
records.summary: Pairs a language model with an evaluator and an evolving database of programs, searching for code that constructs strong solutions. The paper reports new cap-set constructions and improved bin-packing heuristics. Its successes depend on explicit evaluators and problem specifications, making the verification mechanism central to its scientific relevance.

records.name: GPT Researcher
records.summary: A configurable research agent that decomposes questions, gathers evidence from web or local sources, and assembles cited reports. It exposes a package, interfaces, and multi-agent or recursive research workflows. It is useful as a general research component, but its project-level claims should not be confused with scientific novelty or independently validated literature-review completeness.

records.name: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
records.summary: SciMON retrieves semantic, graph and citation-based inspirations to generate scientific idea sentences, then revises suggestions that resemble prior work. Expert studies find improvements over baseline models, but NLP ideas remain substantially less novel and technically detailed than source papers. Evaluations use extracted problem contexts and seed terms; novelty gains are conditional on selected revisions, without executing the proposed research.

records.name: Coscientist
records.summary: Connects language models with literature and documentation search, code execution, and laboratory automation for chemistry tasks. The Nature study demonstrates planning and execution across several experimental settings. The public repository contains supporting data and a simplified implementation, with commercial-use restrictions; it should not be described as a complete unrestricted release of the original laboratory system.

records.name: ASReview LAB
records.summary: Uses active learning to prioritize records during systematic literature screening while preserving human inclusion decisions. It provides a screening interface, simulation tools, label management, and exportable review state. This is a complementary evidence-selection tool rather than a generative scientist; screening completeness depends on the review protocol, labels, and stopping decision.

records.name: The Automation of Science (Robot Scientist Adam)
records.summary: Combines hypothesis generation, automated laboratory experiments, and a logical record of the research process to study yeast functional genomics. The authors report manual confirmation of Adam's conclusions. This pre-LLM example grounds modern autonomy discussions in a closed experimental loop and explicit provenance within a constrained biological problem.
